articleTitle: Improved Remote Sensing Image Target Detection Algorithm Based on YOLOv5
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Remote sensing information processing plays an important role in many fields such as environmental protection, urban planning, military reconnaissance and so on. However, there are problems in remote sensing images such as complex background, large size change, small target, etc. A remote sensing image target detection algorithm to improve YOLOv5 is proposed. Using a certain percentage of data enhancement technology at the input side to enrich the data features and improve the model generalization ability and robustness; for the problem of small targets in remote sensing images, SPD-Conv module is added to reduce the loss of fine-grained information and improve the detection performance of small targets; the design uses the DCNv2 module to replace part of the neck structure of the C3 layer, which breaks through the limitation of traditional convolution and improves the feature extraction ability of the network in remote sensing images. Experimental results show that the improved YOLOv5 model improves the detection accuracy by 3.9%.

articleTitle: Aircraft Control Level Evaluation: Environmental Factor Analysis and Quantitative Evaluation System Construction
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: In the globalized aviation industry, maintaining safety and efficiency presents significant challenges. This study evaluates aircraft control proficiency using real flight data, moving beyond conventional methods. The analysis focuses on four key indicators: stick deflection, rudder deflection, and the positions of the left and right throttle levers, which are used to classify flight control as proper or improper. Environmental factors influencing improper controls are quantified using Pearson correlation analysis and random forest regression. A quantitative evaluation system is then developed using the TOPSIS method with entropy weighting. This innovative, data-driven approach addresses the limitations of traditional methods, offering a comprehensive framework for evaluating aircraft control proficiency.

articleTitle: Research on Fault Diagnosis of Rotating Machinery Based on Multi-Scale Causal Dilation Convolution
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Diagnosing faults in the rolling bearing of rotating machinery equipment is vital to ensuring the stability and safety of industrial production. Traditional convolution-based methods are limited by insufficient extraction of global temporal features. Therefore, this paper proposes a fault diagnosis model for rolling bearings based on multi-scale causal dilated convolution LSTM. This model adopts causal dilated convolution to expand the receptive field while keeping the number of parameters constant, effectively extracting global temporal information from signals, and introduces a multi-scale processing strategy to capture features at different time scales. Furthermore, the LSTM network is utilized to extract temporal dependencies on time series data, enhancing the diagnostic capability of the model for complex vibration signals. Experimental results on the HIT bearing fault dataset show that the proposed model has a significant advantage in fault diagnosis accuracy with an accuracy rate of 98.44%, validating its effectiveness and superiority. Through ablation experiments and comparative experiments, it further confirms the rationality of the model and provides a referable approach for fault diagnosis in rotating machinery equipment.

articleTitle: Design of a Distributed Fusion Network Based on Knowledge Distillation
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Given the outstanding performance of knowledge distillation networks in optimizing traditional deep neural networks, this paper proposes a distributed fusion network based on knowledge distillation. It leverages knowledge distillation techniques to partition the different branches of the distributed fusion network into teacher and student networks. Specifically, the branch modules responsible for extracting feature information from source images are designated as the teacher network, while those extracting feature information from fused images are designated as the student network. Additionally, the designed distillation loss facilitates the transfer of feature information from the teacher network to the student network, enabling the learning of feature information from source images. Extensive experimental results on public datasets demonstrate the model's promising performance in enhancing fusion quality.

articleTitle: Dual-Input Dual-Output Underwater Image Enhancement with Branch Interaction
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Due to the inevitable light absorption and scattering, the quality of underwater images is severely compromised, limiting human exploration of the ocean world. To overcome this challenge, we have developed a Dual-branch interactive dual-input dual-output underwater image enhancement model, termed DBINet, which aims to improve the clarity of underwater images and thus provide strong support for underwater activities. The core of DBINet lies in its dual-branch structure, which can simultaneously process inputs from different underwater images and extract common degradation features from these images. Initially, information extraction is performed using an efficient Transformer block. Then, through the Dual-Branch Skip Layer, we achieve interaction and supplementation of features, further enhancing information in similar regions and thus improving the final image quality. Experimental results confirm the effectiveness of DBINet, significantly enhancing the clarity of underwater images and producing higher-quality enhanced images.

articleTitle: Research on Video Pedestrian Re-ID Method Based on Global Branching and Channel Division
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Pedestrian re-identification is a new technology that has emerged in the field of intelligent detection and analysis in recent years, and is increasingly attracting the attention of researchers. Compared with image-based pedestrian. Re-identification, Video-based pedestrian re-identification has more information. However it is faced with more gradient disappearance or gradient explosion, which makes low efficiency, poor generalization ability, thus leading to low model efficiency. Therefore, this paper proposes a video pedestrian re-identification method based on Channel Division and Global Branching. Firstly, the backbone network of ResNet50 is introduced, and the global feature and Channel Division are combined to comprehensively take into account the global information and feature extraction deepening. Then, the SEWeight module is introduced, whose compression and stimulation parts can be used to encode global information and adaptively recalibrate the channel relationship. Multiple loss functions and activation functions are also used to optimize the model. Finally, extensive experiments have verified the effectiveness of our method, and our method has achieved the most advanced results on two major datasets: Mars and iLDS-VID.

articleTitle: Modified Affinity Propagation for Key Node Identification Based on Intra-Class Distances
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Identifying key nodes is vital to the research of information control in network science and multiagent systems. This paper presents an enhanced affinity propagation clustering algorithm designed to identify critical network nodes by leveraging local and global information. Specifically, we introduce a novel influence matrix, which serves as a standard representation of node relationships. This matrix considers factors such as the number of neighbors and the number of shortest paths, providing a comprehensive view of node importance within the network. The proposed algorithm combines matrix iteration with evaluating local and global network structures to identify key nodes. And intra-class distance is introduced to pinpoint a smaller group of key nodes in large-scale networks. The experimental results on six real networks of different sizes show the validity of identification using the Susceptible-Infected (SI) model and network efficiency.

articleTitle: Integrating Multicore SVM With Enhanced Residual Networks for AI Content Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: This study delves into the intersection of data science and machine learning methodologies, specifically examining the recognition of Artificial Intelligence (AI)-generated papers and images. We curate a comprehensive dataset comprising 200 papers and 855 images, meticulously segregating them into AI-generated and non-AI categories, and transform this raw data into structured formats suitable for rigorous analysis. For text classification, we employ a Multicore Support Vector Machines (SVM) model, optimized through cross-validation and grid search techniques, to accurately distinguish AI-authored papers from human-penned ones. For image classification, we develop an enhanced model that builds upon the strengths of ResNet and DenseNet architectures, achieving high accuracy in discerning AI-generated images. Furthermore, we integrate these two classification systems within a weighted, top-level decision framework, offering a holistic approach to AI content recognition. The proposed methodology and findings offer a novel perspective on AI content detection, with potential applications in copyright protection, academic integrity assessment, and media content monitoring. This research contributes to advancing the state-of-the-art in AI content identification and underscores the importance of robust tools for managing the proliferation of AI-generated content.

articleTitle: Enhanced Multivariate Time Series Regression Prediction Using Temporal Convolution Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Multivariate time series data, which has more complex and multidimensional characteristics compared to univariate data, is used in fields such as urban transportation, power grids, and financial markets. Accurately capturing information and dependencies among multiple time series is crucial for future time variable regression prediction. In this paper, we propose a novel method that utilizes Temporal Convolution Network (TCN) model to fuse multiple convolutional layers and residual connections. Experimental results on the energy consumption dataset from the University of British Columbia (UBC) show that our method stable performance across datasets and outperforms LSTM and ARIMA in some cases.

articleTitle: CA-UNet: A Brain MRI Segmentation Model Based on U-Net with Attention Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Brain tissue segmentation is of paramount importance in the field of medical image processing, as its accuracy directly impacts subsequent diagnosis and treatment processes. However, the intricate structure of brain tissue makes it difficult to achieve precise segmentation. To address these issues, we propose a neural network based on UNet with attention mechanism and context fusion module, named CA-UNet. In the network, a Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) is added in encoder and decoder to enhance the model's feature extraction capabilities. Then, the encoded information is sent to the Multi-scale Context Fusion Module (MCFM) for multi-scale context information fusion. In essence, CA-UNet refines the original UNet by incorporating attention mechanisms to better identify and segment small regions within brain MRI images, making it more effective for medical image analysis tasks. The results of this study indicate that the proposed method achieves an average Dice Similarity Coefficient of 95.77%, with white matter being 96.67%, cortical gray matter being 93.63%, basal ganglia and thalami being 95.00% and ventricular cerebrospinal fluid being 96.79%. The introduction of attention mechanism and contextual fusion module is an effective approach to enhance brain tissue segmentation performance.

articleTitle: Enhancing Barangay Safety: Leveraging Convolutional Neural Networks for Comprehensive Detection of Brawling Incidents in Philippine Barangays
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Street Brawling remains a significant concern within the Philippine and global context, posing a threat to community well-being. While extensively recognized as a major issue affecting the younger generation worldwide, the focus on such incidents has predominantly centered around schools. However, in the barangay setting, brawling incidents pose a distinct challenge that demands attention. This paper delves into the realm of action recognition through Machine Learning, aiming to contribute to the proactive identification and understanding of physical violence within the community. Employing Convolutional Neural Networks, the study focuses on training algorithms to detect actions associated with brawling incidents, including punching, and head hitting. The positive outcomes underscore the effectiveness of Convolutional Neural Networks in recognizing these actions. Leveraging CCTV cameras, the findings present an avenue for preventing and addressing brawling incidents within the barangay, ultimately fostering a safer and more secure community environment.

articleTitle: A New Strategy for Retinal Vessel Segmentation Based on Semi-Dilation Supervised Learning and Boundary Reconstruction
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Automatic segmentation of retinal blood vessels is an important means to assist doctors in quickly diagnosing and preventing eye diseases. However, due to the scale differences between blood vessels and the complexity of blood vessel morphology, the development of automatic retinal vessel segmentation is hindered. In response to these segmentation difficulties, this paper proposes a new method based on semi-dilation supervised learning and vessel boundary reconstruction. By using semi-dilation supervised learning during the pre-training stage, the scale differences between blood vessels are effectively alleviated, and the convolution kernel's perception range of fine blood vessels is expanded. In formal training, the boundary reconstruction network removes redundant blood vessels introduced in pre-training and enhances the ability to determine blood vessel boundaries. Our proposed method was ultimately tested on the DRIVE dataset. The results show that the proposed method achieves good results in segmenting fine blood vessels, with a sensitivity of 84.65%, and the overall segmentation effect is improved, with an AUC of 98.84%. The proposed method effectively solves the problem of ignoring subtle blood vessels caused by scale differences.

articleTitle: An EEG Signal Analysis Method Based on Common Spatial Pattern and Support Vector Machine Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: To solve the problem of EEG signal on feature extraction and low recognition rate, we analyze the characteristics of EEG signal and propose an EEG signal analysis method based on common spatial pattern (CSP) and support vector machine (SVM) algorithms. In this method, we first preprocess the EEG signal by wavelet packet transform (WPT) and extract the specific frequency band signal in the EEG signal. Then the features of the EEG signal are extracted by constructing pair-wise CSP (PW-CSP) filters. Finally, the recognition of the EEG signal was realized by the support vector machine algorithm which optimizes parameter selection by particle swarm optimization (PSO), and the 2008 BCI competition 2A data set was used to verify the classification effect of the algorithm. The experimental results indicated that the classification accuracy of the method may reach up to 93.07%, and the average accuracy is higher than the results of the top two in the 2008 brain-computer interface (BCI) competition. The EEG signal features extracted by this method can reflect the signal characteristics of EEG well, and improve the accuracy of classification, which may assist in the development and application of BCI.

articleTitle: Analysis of Standardized Impedance Models for Electrochemical AC Measurement Based on a Global Heuristic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) is a technique that is widely used in different fields, including corrosion studies, semiconductor science, energy conversion and storage technologies, chemical and biological sensing, and so on. This paper presents the portable impedance measurement system developed by the research group, which employs a system-on-chip (SoC) design and embedded software to address the limitations of personal computers (PCs) and data transmission. The system integrates a graphical user interface (GUI) and local area network (LAN) communication to overcome the challenges posed by these traditional approaches. Furthermore, this paper proposes an automatic analysis platform integrating the EIS modelling method and a global heuristic algorithm, which includes outlier rejection, smoothing filtering and validity verification functions. The system is combined with nine circuit equivalent models to achieve intelligent EIS data fitting, which improves the manual fitting process of Zview software. The experimental test results of the system and platform demonstrate that the power supply noise ripple is minimal and the signal meets expectations in the hardware test. The system stability and accuracy are satisfactory in the software test. In the function and algorithm tests, the data preprocessing significantly enhances the fitting degree of experimental data, and the ECM parameter fitting based on the heuristic global optimization algorithm performs well in terms of stability, accuracy, and runtime with an excellent performance. These results enhance the comprehension and analysis of intricate electrochemical systems, diminish the necessity for manual fitting, and furnish a dependable analytical instrument for electrochemical research and applications.

articleTitle: Improving YOLOv8 for Microbial Object Detection in Microscope Images
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: To address the issues such as large scale variation, edges blurring, high density and overlap of microbial objects in the high-resolution microorganism images, this paper proposes an enhanced object detection model IM-YOLOv8 tailored for microscope images. Firstly, the super token attention is introduced into the Bottleneck module of the CSPLayer for feature extraction. This attention module can capture the global relationship based on super pixels in the early stage of the neural network, and improve the feature discrimination ability, so as to deal with the problem of ambiguity in object boundaries. Secondly, a progressive adaptive feature fusion module is designed to gradually fuse the low-level features to generate more discriminative multi-scale features. Finally, these two modules are assembled into the YOLOv8 model to obtain the enhanced object detection model for microscope images. The experimental results on the AGAR-HR dataset demonstrate that our method is 1.6% and 3.2% higher than YOLOv8 in terms of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{mAP}_{50}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{mAP}_{50:95}$</tex> respectively. In addition, the proposed method possesses a more compact structure, and the model parameters are 16.4 M less than YOLOv8, which proves the superior performance of this method.

articleTitle: DVGN: A Differential Value Guidance Network for Underwater Objects Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Although considerable progress has been made in optical underwater objects detection (UOD) in recent years, the task still faces great challenges due to the complexity of the underwater environment and the mimetic behaviour of underwater objects. Existing deep learning-based models usually do not consider the enhancement of underwater object features, resulting in inefficient UOD. In order to solve the above problems, this paper proposes a plug-and-play Differential Value Guidance Network (DVGN) for arbitrarily embedding into an existing model to improve the recognition performance of the model. The salient features of this paper are: 1) We propose a plug-and-play efficient feature fusion method. It can focus on features at different scales and enhance the recognition capability of objects at different scales underwater. 2) Through a large number of experiments, it is proved that it can be embedded into different object detection algorithms to effectively improve the object detection capability with the smallest possible increase model parameters.

articleTitle: SSMask: Salient Super-Pixel Mask Data Augmentation for Object Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Data augmentation is a widely used regularization method to improve the robustness of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) by alleviating the over-fitting problems. In this paper, we propose a heuristic data augmentation scheme for object detection task, termed Salient Super-pixel Mask (SSMask), which exploits the saliency to determine the most discriminative information and achieve the balance between information removal and preservation by the number of seeds of super-pixel segmentation. Concretely, we first obtain sub-regions of an input image by the super-pixel segmentation operator. Then, the static saliency detection algorithm is utilized to compute the saliency map. The most discriminative region can be determined by the combination of super-pixel segmentation and saliency map. Lastly, a region removal mask is built by removing the most discriminative super-pixel region. The data augmentation scheme will be randomly applied to the training stage. Extensive experiments are performed on the Pascal VOC dataset. The mean Average Precision (mAP) of RetinaNet is boosted from 81.59% to 83.14%. The mAP of CenterNet is improved from 81.84% to 84.13%, and the mAP of FCOS is boosted from 79.10% to 83.11%. Experimental results prove the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Research on Match Competition Prediction Algorithm Based on LightGBM
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: With the advent of the era of big data, artificial intelligence and machine learning have developed rapidly. At present, there are many competitive competition data, which can objectively predict the level of players in the future through data analysis. Firstly, based on the data of Wimbledon men's singles in 2023, this paper preprocesses and constructs the index system, and carries out the consistent processing and correlation analysis of the indicators. Among them, player 1 serve depth, player 1 serve speed, player 2 serve speed, player 1 break success rate, player 2 break success rate are the most positively correlated, and finally 5 indicators are determined. Then, the LightGBM prediction algorithm is established to train the 185 games data of five matches, and the results of 42 games in the next game are predicted. The prediction accuracy is 83.72%. Compared with the random forest algorithm and ridge regression, the prediction algorithm has the highest accuracy. Finally, the LightGBM prediction competition fluctuation model was applied to other players, and it was found that the prediction accuracy of the model was 86.21 %. The prediction results show that the generalization effect of LightGBM algorithm is better, which provides a scientific basis for the level prediction of players in competitive competitions.

articleTitle: Label Defect Detection Based on Improved CenterNet
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Defects in labeling represent a prevalent issue that significantly impacts product quality during the manufacturing process. In response to the challenges associated with the detection of label stain defects, this research introduces an enhanced version of the CenterNet algorithm, termed Improved CenterNet. This novel approach predicts the centroid of the object, the diagonal length, and the sine value, which collectively contribute to the optimization of the loss function. This innovation effectively mitigates the problem of disproportionately large loss values, facilitating the accurate estimation of the object's dimensions. When compared to the conventional CenterNet, the Improved CenterNet algorithm not only preserves real-time performance but also markedly enhances the precision and robustness of the detection process. By integrating a sine value prediction mechanism, the algorithm demonstrates a heightened capacity to discern stains against intricate background contexts. Empirical findings indicate that the Improved CenterNet algorithm yields superior performance on a dataset of label stain defects, fulfilling the industrial demand for high-efficiency and high-accuracy defect detection in the manufacturing sector.

articleTitle: Enhancing Embedded System Performance with an Adaptive Quantization Scheme for Binary Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: In order to deploy neural network models on resource-constrained embedded devices, floating-point neural network models need to be quantized into integer networks. Binary neural network is to quantize the activation/weights of the neural network model into 1 bit ({0,1} or {-1,1}). Since binary neural network saves a lot of storage cost and computational resource consumption, it is a promising technique for deploying deep neural networks on embedded devices. However, since there are only two possibilities for each parameter, binary neural network inevitably suffers from a severe loss of information, and optimising the binary neural network becomes difficult due to its discontinuities. The existing binary quantization studies have only been conducted at the level of simulated computational quantization, lacking validation on real hardware. In fact, the binary quantization methods that can really achieve significant acceleration effects on embedded devices by combining the device characteristics are of higher application value and research significance. In this paper, an adaptive quantization method for deploying binary neural networks on embedded systems is proposed, which can significantly improve the deployment accuracy of the binary neural network model on embedded systems.

articleTitle: Weapon Detection using Mask R-CNN and ResNeXt
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: We are living in an era marked by security challenges. Traditional surveillance systems are struggling to keep up with new ways of doing crime. The development of advanced weapon detection system has become important in fight against crime. In this study, a weapon detector system using the Mask Region Convolutional Neural Network (Mask R-CNN) algorithm with ResNeXt as a backbone architecture is proposed. We replace the default Mask R-CNN backbone with ResNext to improve the quality of the features extracted because of ResNext's good cardinality and grouped convolutions. The model generates a high quality segmentation mask for each object instance in the image. The system uses the COCO dataset to get pictures of weapons. We evaluated our system using various performance metrics, our experimental results shows that combination of R-CNN and ResNeXt is one of the most effective ways to detect weapons.

articleTitle: Short-Term Power Load Forecasting Model Based on EEMD-SE-ERCNN
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Given the strong nonlinearity and multiple influencing factors in power load data, this paper proposes a forecasting method based on ensemble empirical mode decomposition (EEMD), sample entropy (SE), and an enhanced residual convolutional neural network (ERCNN). First, EEMD is used to decompose historical loads into several simplified subsequences. Next, Sample Entropy (SE) is introduced to calculate the entropy values of the subsequences, and subsequences with similar entropy values are reconstructed into random, detailed, low-frequency, and trend components. Then, ERCNN with different structures are used to forecast different types of components. Finally, the different components are superimposed to obtain the final forecasting results. Experimental results show that the proposed model outperforms existing models in terms of forecasting performance, with the forecasting error reduced by up to 1.62%, 178.4 MW, and 272.8 MW compared to existing deep learning models.

articleTitle: Digital Circuit Correlation Optimization of Neural Networks for Apnea Detection during Transplantation
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Sleep apnea syndrome (SAS) is a dangerous and high incidence sleep disorder. As more and more people are affected by SAS, monitoring SAS in family life becomes increasingly important. It is very meaningful to design an automatic SAS monitoring device. We designed a SAS detection model based on neural network, and transplanted the model to an application specific integrated circuit (ASIC). There are many problems in the process of transplanting neural network to ASIC. One of the most serious problems is the transplantation of nonlinear activation functions. We proposed a software-hardware joint optimization method to solve the problem of activation function in the SAS model transplantation. In the process of building the neural network model, our research modified the activation function in the traditional LSTM model and the attention mechanism, and adopted hard-sigmoid and LeakyReLU activation function for digital circuits. In the hardware transplantation, the activation function was constructed using the binary shift-based division, three-segment and two-segment function. A digital circuit without migration errors can be obtained with a small area and time consumption. We jointly optimized the structure of the model design and the digital circuit implementation. The model was more suitable for the digital circuit structure, so that the neural network can be transplanted more smoothly.

articleTitle: Non-destructive Detection of Moldy Camellia Oleifera Seeds Based on Deep Learning and Hyperspectral Imaging
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Camellia oleifera, a woody oil plant of high economic value, faces potential mold growth during storage and transportation, which could significantly impact its sales and processing. Therefore, it is crucial to identify and select moldy camellia oleifera seeds. Due to the fact that the mold growth of camellia oleifera seeds typically originates from the inside of the seeds, the mold is not visibly apparent on the surface of the shells in the early stages of mold growth. The existing chemical methods are time-consuming, labor-intensive, and result in sample damage. To address this challenge, this study introduces a non-destructive detection method for assessing the extent of mold growth in camellia oleifera seeds efficiently and effectively. The method is based on deep learning and hyperspectral imaging (HSI) technology. A hyperspectral imaging system was utilized to capture hyperspectral images of camellia oleifera seeds at three degrees of mold. In response to the limitations of traditional machine learning methods in hyperspectral classification, which only focus on learning spectral features and yield unsatisfactory results, this study introduces a deep learning approach based on three-dimensional convolution. This algorithm is capable of extracting features from both spatial and spectral information. The classification performance of the proposed model is compared with machine learning methods that rely solely on spectral information and deep learning methods that use only spatial information from visual images. Based on the dataset constructed in this study, experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves an accuracy of 88.99%, surpassing other methods by at least 18.6%.

articleTitle: Development an Object Tracking Method Based on Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Object tracking based on deep learning is a challenging task. Accurate object detection and tracking requires a neural network that is deeper than a typical network. Therefore, it requires more levels of processing and takes more time. The YOLO model is considered one of the most state-of-the-art neural networks. Its wide application in object tracking depends on the speed of processing and extracting object features. In this article, we develop the YOLO model by changing the final layer from a fully connected layer to a fully convolutional layer, changing the activation function, and adding a batch normalization layer. A comparison of the results with the old YOLO model shows improved accuracy and speed. Additionally, the developed model is less sensitive to noisy environments.

articleTitle: Simulation Study on Optimization of ZigBee Routing Protocol Based on Improved Cluster Tree Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: In order to solve the problem of high energy consumption, low routing efficiency, and long network delay in the two main routing algorithm. The paper proposed an improved cluster tree algorithm that combinated the routing algorithms of AODVjr and cluster tree. Based on the basic ZigBee routing algorithm, classified the routing algorithms of AODVjr and cluster tree. basic ZigBee routing algorithm, classified the routing nodes according to the residual energy of the nodes, and simplified the algorithm process, used the characteristics of data transmission as the basis of alternative routing algorithm. The simulation results showed that the improved cluster tree algorithm performance better. The simulation results showed that the improved cluster tree algorithm had better performance. However, the delay of improved cluster tree algorithm would be slightly larger when the number of nodes were same, and it had better performance in energy balance, achieved the purposes of energy optimization, met the requirements of low cost, low energy consumption, high reliability of wireless sensor networks. high reliability of wireless sensor networks.

articleTitle: A Redundant Data Elimination Method Based on Change Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: In recent years, with the rapid development of aerospace technology, the variety of satellite payloads has increased, and the volume of remote sensing data has become increasingly massive. These changes have also put forward higher requirements for the functionality and performance of storage systems. Starting from the perspective of the content validity of image data, this paper proposes a redundant data elimination method based on change detection. By using a twin fully convolutional neural network to implement change detection for remote sensing images of the same scene at different times, and based on the change detection results, adopting certain strategies to eliminate unchanged areas, the method maximizes the elimination of redundant information in remote sensing data without losing effective information, thereby reducing the volume of stored data. The experimental results have verified the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Design and Development of VR Virtual Chinese Painting Based on Unity3D
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: In the past two decades, with the rapid updates and iterations of computer graphics and assisted drawing technology, people have been able to create various art works that were previously difficult to complete. However, many Chinese people have become unfamiliar with the traditional art form of traditional Chinese painting, and more modern things are drowning it out. In the face of such a situation, using modern technology to express traditional Chinese painting in innovative forms can be a means for people to refocus their attention on traditional Chinese painting. There have been some attempts in the past decade, but the final presentation has mostly been done on ordinary monitors, with few cases of using virtual reality technology. Virtual reality technology provides two images with subtle differences in observation angles to the eyes, allowing the human brain to intuitively perceive the three-dimensional world and achieve dimensionality enhancement in presentation. This paper introduces the design and development process of a project that models several selected traditional Chinese paintings created by renowned artist Zhang Daqian in a virtual reality development environment, incorporates dynamic and interactive elements, and cleverly integrates them into a 3D scene.

articleTitle: Global Sensitivity Analysis and Parameter Calibration for a Mechanism-Based Forecasting Model of Rice Sheath Blight Disease
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Variations in environmental conditions and disease epidemic characteristics across regions pose challenges for effectively applying disease forecasting models. To address this issue, this paper proposes a novel approach combining global sensitivity analysis and uncertainty quantification for model calibration: (1) The extended fourier amplitude sensitivity test (EFAST) is employed to identify key parameters of the crop disease forecasting model; (2) These critical parameters are calibrated using the generalized likelihood uncertainty estimation (GLUE) method to adapt the model for regional-scale forecasting. The results showed that the sensitivity of the output variables did not change with the changes of crop parameters, and the basic infection rate (b) and average latency time (w) showed sensitivity to the plants' infection rate relative to other parameters when the parameter fluctuations ranged from 5% to 25%. Secondly, the actual and forecasted plants' infection rate simulated by the model after calibration was in good agreement, with the RMSE decreasing to 8.71 and R2 increasing to 0.7 compared to the model calibrated by the genetic algorithm.

articleTitle: Feature Aggregation and Mixing via Cross Attention for Nuclei Instance Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Nuclei instance segmentation aims to identify individual nuclei within histopathological images, playing a crucial role in various medical image analysis tasks such as cancer diagnosis and treatment planning. However, this task encounters challenges such as densely clustered nuclei, blurry boundaries, overlapping regions, and variations in shape and size across different organs, leading to the erroneous separation of individual nuclei. In recent years, transformer architecture has achieved commendable performance in medical image segmentation due to its ability to efficiently capture global contextual information. However, its inherent design limits its ability to capture fine-grained local information within images, thereby restricting its full potential. To address this limitation, we propose a novel transformer-based method and design two effective modules, a multi-scale feature aggregation module (MSFAM) and a feature-mixing cross-attention module (FMCAM). These modules are specifically designed to aggregate feature maps by capturing fine-grained information and enhancing contextual details through mixing feature maps of various scales via cross attention. Furthermore, to separate each nucleus, we add an additional branch to predict horizontal and vertical distance maps to obtain boundary information, thereby enabling the distinction of each nucleus. We evaluate the proposed method on the multi-organ nuclei segmentation (MoNuSeg) dataset. Experimental results demonstrate that our method achieves outstanding performance in the nuclei instance segmentation task.

articleTitle: A Lightweight CNN-Transformer Network with Agent Attention Mechanism for 3D Whole Heart Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: In recent years, heart diseases have become one of the major global health issues, emphasizing the importance of 3D whole heart segmentation technology for accurate and efficient treatment. Currently, 3D whole heart segmentation algorithms often combine Transformer technologies with 3D Convolutional Neural Networks (3D CNNs), leveraging the self-attention mechanism of Transformers for global information modeling and 3D CNNs for capturing local contextual information. However, the high computational complexity of Transformers leads to huge computational resource wastage. To address this issue, this work proposes a novel whole heart segmentation algorithm named AgentTransBTS, based on an improved 3D Agent Attention mechanism and the TransBTS framework. This algorithm utilizes TransBTS as the baseline model, capitalizing on its deep feature extraction and information integration capabilities to capture global dependencies in images. To reduce computational complexity without sacrificing the model's expressive power, an enhanced 3D Agent Attention mechanism is introduced. Comprehensive experiments were conducted on the Multi-Modality Whole Heart Segmentation (MM-WHS) 2017 dataset to evaluate the proposed algorithm. The experimental results demonstrate that our proposed method achieved an average Dice coefficient of 91.9% on the CT dataset and 79.9% on the MRI dataset of the MM-WHS 2017 challenge. Furthermore, our algorithm's FLOPs are 217G, representing an approximate 9.2% improvement in computational efficiency compared to the baseline network.

articleTitle: Pretrained Model with CNN for Lung Cancer Identification and Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Lung cancer impacts both genders, and its early detection is key to lowering death rates. Current deep learning techniques for automated identification and classification of lung carcinoma face issues with interpretability, data variability handling, and broader applicability. In our research, we propose a novel method that merges a convolutional neural network (CNN) with a streamlined RESNET18 framework. This approach is designed for lung cancer detection and categorization from CT scans, involving image preprocessing like resizing and rescaling. It effectively differentiates between healthy and cancerous tissues, further classifying them as either Normal, Benign, or Malignant, including variants such as adenocarcinoma and squamous cell carcinoma. Our CNN+RESNET18 model boasts an impressive 99% accuracy, supporting radiologists in the intricate task of image analysis, reducing risks of incorrect or delayed diagnosis, and fostering prompt treatment for improved patient outcomes.

articleTitle: Improved YOLOv8 Detection Algorithm of Contraband in X-Ray Security Inspection Image
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Personnel safety is particularly important in public places where security checks are required, such as airports, train stations and subway stations. In view of the features of disorderly placement of items, blocking of contraband and intentional hiding in X-ray security inspection images, this research proposes an improved YOLOv8 network model combined with Mixup data augmentation, Biformer dual-layer routing attention modules, and C2f_f modules to assist security personnel in conducting efficient security inspections. At the input stage, the Mixup data augmentation method is employed to enhance the model's ability to learn to detect obstructed and concealed prohibited items. The Biformer dual-layer routing attention modules are introduced into the backbone network to enhance the model's focus on foreground information and improve its recognition ability. The C2f_f modules are incorporated into the backbone network and Neck section to improve the model's feature representation capability and enhance overall network performance. Testing on the Easy, Hard, and Hidden datasets of PIDray yields mAPs of 85.2%, 86.2%, and 68.3% respectively. Experimental results demonstrate an increased detection accuracy of 2.3%, 1.4%, and 2.2% respectively on the three prohibited item recognition test sets for the improved YOLOv8 model.

articleTitle: Dual Convolutional Neural Network with Explainability Attention Mechanism for Diabetic Retinopathy Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is a worldwide chronic eye disease which is a complication due to long-term diabetes. DR can gradually reduce a patient's vision and even lead to blindness. Therefore, in order to effectively prevent potential retinopathy, early diagnosis and timely intervention are particularly important. In recent years, with the rapid development of deep learning technology, convolutional neural network (CNN) has become an important analysis tool in the medical field. In this study, we propose a novel dual convolutional neural network model that combines the Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) to enhance the feature extraction capability. Specifically, we fused the network “PD-NET” based on null convolution and pyramid pooling and the network “ResDSCM-NET” based on deeply separable convolution and multi-scale convolution to construct the final ensemble model. In order to verify the effectiveness of the proposed model, we conducted experiments using the DR dataset. The experimental results show that the model achieves 96.38% accuracy in detecting DR, which is significantly better than the existing methods. The results indicate that the proposed model has high accuracy and potential for early diagnosis of DR and is expected to play an important role in clinical applications.

articleTitle: TUTNet - A Segmentation Network for Fabric Sewing Thread in the Texture Background
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Sewing thread segmentation can help locate the defects in fabric sewing process, which is a challenging problem in factory quality control. In this paper, we propose a twin U-shaped Transformer Network (TUTNet) for sewing thread segmentation. To learn high-dimensional abstract features and capture the sewing direction while ensuring the smoothness of segmentation, we propose a Twin-Attention Module (TAM), which is composed of Sewing Thread Direction (STD) and Sewing Thread Smoothness (STS) blocks. To better combine low-dimensional features with fine-grained features, and generate more continuous results, we propose a Scaled Feature Fusion Module (SFFM), which is used to calculate losses at multiple levels. We also propose a large-scale sewing thread segmentation (STSeg) dataset, which is collected from real clothing production factory. Finally, we conduct experiments on both STSeg and DGRE datasets to verify the effectiveness of our method for sewing thread and other linear object segmentation.

articleTitle: Research on Automatic Detection of Epileptic Seizures Based on the CNN-Transformer Model
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Epilepsy is a severe brain disorder affecting approximately 50 million people worldwide. Given that the sudden onset of epileptic seizures can be quite serious, the detection of such seizures is crucial. Clinically, scalp electroencephalography (EEG) is commonly used as a non-invasive method to diagnose and identify the seizure foci in epilepsy, but manually interpreting EEGs is time-consuming and labor-intensive, which has driven the need for automated methods. To improve this, we have proposed a new framework that incorporates deep learning. This framework utilizes Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) to process multi-channel EEG data, extracting temporal and spatial information, while leveraging Transformer encoders to capture complex sequential data. On the public EEG epilepsy detection dataset TUSZ, our method achieved a weighted average F1 score of 0.778, as well as a precision of 0.808 and sensitivity of 0.769, showing significant results. Additionally, we have developed an epilepsy seizure detection system based on our model, which automatically assesses whether an epileptic seizure is occurring based on uploaded EEG files and implements warning responses.

articleTitle: Feature Level Fusion of Radar and Camera based on Transformer in 3D Object Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: In the field of 3D object perception, millimeter-wave radar and cameras have complementary information. However, the sparseness of millimeter-wave radar point clouds and the differences in camera and radar data make it difficult to fuse the features of the two sensors. In order to achieve further correlation between radar and cameras, much research has been invested in camera-radar fusion 3D object detection. We propose a new radar point cloud processing network and a feature-level fusion method based on Tranformer, which uses radar point to supplement camera information at a fast inference speed to achieve effective radar camera fusion. The input of the radar network does not need to exclude invalid radar points in advance, and the unstructured and disordered radar point cloud after clustering is directly input. The output not only includes the information carried by the radar point, but also obtains the structural information between radar groups. The fusion network obtains refined detection results through interactive fusion of features. The entire model structure is simple and no manual methods are used in network inference. Compared with the single-view method, this method improved by 5.3% on NDS, and the errors in orientation, translation, velocity and attributes were reduced.

articleTitle: Improved YOLOv8 for Small Aircraft Detection in SAR Images
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: There are many small and medium-sized object instances and strong background interference in SAR image, which is easy to cause missed detection and misdetection. To solve this problem, this paper proposes an aircraft detection algorithm based on improved YOLOv8. Firstly, the YOLOv8 network is reconstructed to add shallow feature detection heads to retain more details and enhance the algorithm's ability to capture small objects. Secondly, the C2f_DualConv module is designed to improve the information processing and feature extraction ability of the model while reducing the calculation cost and the number of parameters. Thirdly, Slim-Neck structure is introduced to improve the feature utilization efficiency of the model. Finally, the ASFF mechanism is used to improve the detection head and improve the scale invariance of the features. Experimental results on the SAR-AIRcraft-1.0 dataset show that the precision rate, recall rate and mAP50 of the proposed algorithm are respectively improved by 3.1%, 1.1% and 0.9% compared with the original YOLOv8 algorithm. Compared with the current mainstream object detection algorithms, the proposed algorithm can effectively improve the detection accuracy, and significantly improve the missed and false detection of aircrafts, and is more suitable for the task of small aircraft detection in SAR images.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Anti-Peeping Screen Algorithm Based on Soft-NMS YOLOv7
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: The occurrence of privacy breaches through screen peeping has highlighted the increasing importance of anti-peeping screen algorithms. In the traditional YOLOv7 algorithm, it may not accurately detect faces when individuals are mutually obscured. In order to improve the success rate of face detection, we propose a new anti-peeping screen algorithm, Soft-NMS-YOLOv7. Compared to the traditional NMS-YOLOv7, Soft-NMS-YOLOv7 prevents face leakage by specially handling the scores of adjacent detection boxes. Therefore, Soft-NMS-YOLOv7 exhibits better detection performance and robustness, increasing the accuracy of face detection in anti-peeping screen algorithms from 90.05% to 94.71%. Additionally, we have developed a physical model of Soft-NMS-YOLOv7 based on Raspberry Pi 4B.

articleTitle: UW-DETR: Underwater Image Instance Segmentation with Co-DETR
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Underwater image instance segmentation is crucial for marine environmental protection and management. However, the light scattering effect of the underwater environment can reduce the image quality and blur the boundaries of objects, which can significantly impair the performance of underwater instance segmentation. Furthermore, there are organisms that are camouflaged underwater and can perfectly blend into the underwater environment. To address these issues, we propose UW-DETR, a Co-DETR-based instance segmentation model for underwater images. Firstly, the Boundary Aware Module (BAM) to generate a priori edge information, thereby providing effective edge information in underwater images. Subsequently, the a priori edge information is combined with the feature maps, which serves to enhance the model's boundary perception, reduce the impact of scattering effects on the image, and improve the detection of camouflaged targets, thereby aiding the model's prediction. Secondly, we were inspired by the Boundary Learning Loss (BLL) in WaterMask, which highlighted the importance of boundary loss in underwater instance segmentation tasks. However, BLL does not consider the boundary loss of underwater camouflaged targets, so we improved on BLL and proposed Multiple Boundary Losses (MBL) to guide the model to produce more accurate results. A series of experiments conducted on the UIIS dataset demonstrated that our method achieved a mean average precision (mAP) of 29.2 using ResNet-101 as the backbone, representing an improvement of 2AP over the WaterMask R-CNN.

articleTitle: Advanced Modulation Recognition with CResNet for Mining Complex Information
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Automatic modulation recognition is a key technology in the field of cognitive radio, which plays an important role in civil and military fields. In recent years, the increasing number of signal modulation types and the increasing complexity of the communication electromagnetic environment have brought great challenges to automatic modulation identification. In this paper, we introduce a novel automatic modulation recognition (AMR) system, the Complex-convolution Residual Network (CResNet), tailored for accurately identifying modulation modes in challenging low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) conditions. This model incorporates a complex module at the input layer to capture the key comple features of radio signals, including signal phase and amplitude nuances. Key enhancements include the use of complex Adam optimizer, which bolster feature discernment of the complex radio signal. Our evaluation on the RadioML2016.10a dataset demonstrates robust performance across SNR levels, achieving a notable 0.59 average all-SNR accuracy and over 0.82 accuracy in >0 dB environment. It shows superior performance compared to traditional and contemporary AMR models, particularly in challenging low SNR conditions, highlighting the model's robustness and adaptability in complex electromagnetic environments, providing a solid foundation for future research and applications in advanced complex signal processing and recognition tasks.

articleTitle: CSM2Net: Exploring Effective Fusion of Complex Spectral Masking and Complex Spectral Mapping for Speech Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Speech enhancement is essential to front-end speech signal processing, which can effectively improve speech quality and clarity. Complex spectral masking and complex spectral mapping are the main methods for speech enhancement in the time-frequency domain. This paper proposes a novel fusing complex spectral masking and complex spectral mapping networks (CSM2Net) to combine both advantages. The complex spectral masking and spectral mapping branches share the same encoder and interact in the decoding stage through a dual-branch cross-attention block. In the encoding and decoding stage, a novel soft-threshold attention block extracts speech time-frequency features and makes the model focus on more critical features. Finally, the outputs of the two branches are fused by a weight-generating block, which efficiently selects the better spectrum. On the test set, CSM2Net achieves advanced performance using almost minimal model parameters compared to other state-of-the-art models.

articleTitle: Object Detection Model of YOLOv8-CSD for UAV Images
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: In order to address the challenges faced in detecting objects in UAV aerial images, we propose an enhanced YOLOv8-CSD object detection algorithm. Our aim is to overcome issues such as low accuracy, complex model structure, limited generalization ability, small size of detected objects, variations in scale and occlusion due to background elements. These factors often lead to missed detections and false alarms. To improve the feature extraction capability and enhance detection accuracy, we introduce the SimAM attention mechanism into the network's neck section. Additionally, we leverage the benefits offered by deformable convolutional networks and incorporate a C2fDCN module into the YOLOv8 neck network for improved feature fusion ability specifically targeting small targets. Furthermore, we replace the original detection head with DyHead for unified scale consideration along with spatial and task awareness. Experimental results on VisDrone2019 dataset consisting of aerial photography demonstrate that our improved algorithm achieves a mean Average Precision (mAP) of 41.9%, which is 3.4% higher than that achieved by the original YOLOv8s algorithm. This showcases excellent performance while validating its effectiveness.

articleTitle: A Spatial Small Object Detection Algorithm Based on the Improved YOLOv8
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: In spatial object detection tasks, due to the far observation distance, objects often exist in the form of point objects. Due to the extremely small size of the object, the number of detectable objects is very limited, which can easily lead to missed detection and false positives in object detection. To solve these issues, we proposes a spatial object detection algorithm based on the improved YOLOv8. This algorithm enhances the network's feature extraction ability by adding GAM Attention to the Neck part of the YOLOv8 object detection algorithm, reduces information reduction, and magnifies the global interactive representations to improve the performance of deep neural networks and reduce the interference of background noise in small object detection tasks in complex environments. It introduces 3D permutation and multilayer perceptron to achieve channel attention and a convolutional spatial attention submodule to better capture the detail information of small objects. The experimental results show that the improved YOLOv8 algorithm has improved the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{mAP_{50}}$</tex> by 1.3%, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{mAP_{50-95}}$</tex> by 1.9% on the ISS dataset. In conclusion, the improved YOLOv8 can enhance the performance of small object detection.

articleTitle: The Construction and Experimental Technologies of Anonymous Network Analysis and Control Platform
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: In view of the shortcomings of low accuracy and high false positive rate in the traditional anonymous network traffic analysis methods, this paper proposes the construction and experimental technologies of the anonymous network analysis and control platform, and adopts the Tor network forced routing mechanism to realize the reverse analysis of the random path selection and proxy data restoration of the anonymous network. Experimental results show that compared with the traditional anonymous network traffic analysis methods, the anonymous network analysis and control platform significantly improves performance, achieving a true positive rate of over 95% for detecting different types of traffic in anonymous networks and a false positive rate of less than 3%. This approach not only reduces the overhead of training the model but also enhances the generalization ability of anonymous network analysis and control.

articleTitle: A Domain Knowledge Graph Construction Method Based on Joint Extraction of GlobalPointer
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: In order to reduce the effect of ternary overlap on the joint extraction, the GlobalPointer global pointer joint extraction strategy is used to construct a vertical domain knowledge map. The method maps the inputs into embedding vectors through the BERT pre-training model and transmits them to the Transformer bi-directional encoder to obtain dynamic word vectors that can characterize the polysemy of words. Then the idea of GlobalPointer global normalization is applied to consider the first and last information of the entity, and the first and last information of the recognized entity is introduced as a whole to be predicted, and the ternary extraction is transformed into quintuple extraction to realize the joint decoding of the information. Finally, the test is carried out on the DuIE public dataset, and the results show that compared with the mainstream TPLinker, CasRel and other baseline models, the proposed model performs the best in terms of F1 scores, and the comprehensive F1 value reaches 82.62%.

articleTitle: Fiber Optic Sensor Demodulation System Using Peak Wavelength Tracking Method and Neural Network Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Fiber optic sensors are used to measure various physical quantities because of their excellent characteristics. This paper proposes a fiber optic sensor demodulation system for temperature and barometric pressure measurement using an artificial neural network. The fiber optic sensor uses the structure of a fiber Bragg grating tandem Fabry-Perot interferometer, which is used to convert changes in temperature and barometric pressure in the environment into changes in the peak wavelength of the reflected spectrum. The demodulation system uses an artificial neural network to establish the nonlinear relationship between the peak spectral wavelength and the temperature and pressure to achieve the demodulation of the fiber optic sensor. An effective data augmentation method is used to train the neural network model to guarantee the demodulation performance even for small experimental data. The experimental results show that the average demodulation error of this system is 0.48 °C for temperature and 13.38kPa for barometric pressure, and the demodulation performance is better than the traditional wavelength tracking demodulation system. This paper provides a practical reference scheme for neural network application in fiber optic sensing demodulation.

articleTitle: Design a Hybrid Neural Network Tracking System Using Multiple Cameras
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Neural networks have become a transformative technology, enabling significant advances over the past few decades. In particular, detection and tracking systems benefit from the ability of neural networks to learn and extract features, resulting in accurate object classification and localization. In this paper, we propose a hybrid neural network framework that integrates data from multiple cameras positioned along an object's path. This multi-camera configuration expands the system's field of view and improves prediction accuracy when tracking an object's position. We conduct extensive experiments to evaluate the performance of our proposed model, which demonstrates superior tracking accuracy and robustness across different environments compared to traditional single-camera systems.

articleTitle: Rapider-YOLOv7: Lightweight Infrared Object Detection Network
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: YOLOv7-tiny, as a lightweight variant of YOLOv7, boasts advantages of fast runtime and fewer parameters. However, when directly applied to infrared object detection, YOLOv7-tiny still faces challenges such as weak extraction of fine details, loss of semantic information, and high resource consumption. To address these issues, we propose a comprehensive balance between detection speed and accuracy in the Rapider-YOLOv7 object detection network. Firstly, it introduces the Exponential Spatial Pyramid Pooling with Channel Spatial Pyramid (Soft-SPPCSP) module to enhance the capability of the original model in extracting low contrast information from infrared images. Secondly, it designs the FO-CA attention module to strengthen the model's feature extraction capability for infrared images with weak textures. Furthermore, it devises the lightweight SFaster-net network, which incorporates SPDconv convolution for feature extraction to accelerate the model's feature extraction speed and enhance its capability to extract features from low-resolution images. Experimental results on the FLIR-v2 infrared dataset demonstrate that the mAP of the Rapider-YOLOv7 model reaches 62.6%, which is 2.9% higher than that of the original YOLOv7-tiny. Moreover, the FPS value on the RTX4060ti reaches 93.

articleTitle: End-to-End Network for Early Crop Planting Area Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Early prediction of crop planting areas is essential for agricultural planning and management. Traditional two-stage calculation methods face limitations due to remote sensing imagery classification and are prone to significant area predicting errors due to ‘error accumulation.’ This paper introduces an innovative end-to-end network designed for accurate, large-scale early-stage crop area prediction. Leveraging multi-subimages processing and ‘trusted pixel’ technology, our approach overcomes the technical challenges of conventional methods, by extracting features from multi-year land cover data, our model directly predicts crop planting areas. Experiments on estimating corn and soybean areas in the USA show a relative error below 4%. Our research lays a foundation for early-stage crop monitoring, supports sustainable agricultural practices, and provides actionable insights for agricultural decision-making and resource allocation.

articleTitle: Algorithm Improvement for Bacterial Detection in Microfluidic Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: In this work, we applied a combination of microfluidic chip technology and microscopic imaging to observe bacterial growth under antibiotic influence allows for faster and more accurate assessment of antibiotic efficacy against bacteria, which is crucial for clinical diagnosis and prevention of antibiotic misuse. This study proposes an algorithm improvement method for E. coli detection on a microfluidic platform based on YOLOv8, which effectively addressed issues such as missed detections in small target detection like bacteria. Firstly, a dense connection mechanism is introduced in the C2f module. Secondly, Attention-based Intra-scale Feature Interaction is added deep within the backbone to enhance the model's capability in recognizing and localizing small targets. Additionally, an iterative attention-based multi-scale feature fusion method is incorporated into the Neck, which not only reduces computational costs but also allows the model to focus more on relevant features, minimizing interference from redundant information. In image preprocessing, we applied contrast limited adaptive histogram equalization to the captured bacterial images. According to experimental results, the model has improved mAP by approximately 10% after preprocessing the bacterial images. Compared to the Baseline, the improved model achieved a slight decrease in accuracy but increased recall and mAP@0.5 by 5.4% and 2.4%, respectively.

articleTitle: Improved Yolov5 Photovoltaic Panel Defect Detection Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Aiming at the problem of low detection accuracy in photovoltaic panel defect detection, which exists in the defects with different shapes, complex and variable background texture, this paper proposes an improved yolov5s network model containing RepNCSPELAN4 module and CARAFE module. Firstly, the RepNCSPELAN4 module is used to replace the C3 layer in the trunk and neck to enrich the feature extraction capability of the network and improve the feature expression capability of the network. Secondly, the content-aware feature reorganisation module CARAFE is introduced to handle multi-scale information and contextual information more effectively and improve the accuracy of prediction. Compared with the original yolov5s network, the improved model shows a 2.1 % increase in mAP with a 19.2% reduction in the number of parameters. The results show that the improved yolov5s detection model can effectively locate and identify EL defect images of PV cells.

articleTitle: SE-ResNet: Recognition of ECG Anomalies Based on Convolutional Neural Network with Fused Attention
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: As the most widely used approaches for observing cardiovascular disease in clinical medicine, electrocardiogram (ECG) signal can accurately reflect the physiological state of the heart. However, the unified processing of one-dimensional ECG signal is limited by the different supplies and communication protocols of ECG equipment. In this paper, we propose an image-based ECG anomaly detection method that achieves a unified processing mode through signal to image conversion. To this end, we first convert the one-dimension 12-lead ECG signal into the two-dimension image type. Then, an ECG anomaly classification mode named SE-ResNet is built by the ResNet architecture and a channel attention mechanism is utilized to enhance the feature extraction ability. Lastly, extensive experiments are conducted on a simulated clinical 12-lead ECG image dataset. The classification accuracy and F1 score of the proposed method reach 85.69% and 84.51%. Compared with the baseline method, the classification accuracy and F1 score are improved by 1.08% and 1.03% respectively. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Improved Self-Attention for Spodoptera Frugiperda Larval Instar Stages Identification
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Spodoptera frugiperda (fall armyworm, FAW) is a pest that poses a significant threat to global agriculture, with its larvae exhibiting unique morphological characteristics and varying degrees of harm at different instar stages. This study proposes a method that incorporates an improved self-attention mechanism to achieve rapid and accurate identification of FAW larval instars. This method can be seamlessly integrated into convolutional neural networks (CNNs), enhancing recognition performance by focusing on the global features of images. Furthermore, this research has constructed an image dataset of FAW larvae at various developmental stages under field and laboratory conditions to validate the effectiveness of the proposed method. Experimental results demonstrate that our method improves the recognition accuracy across various CNN architectures, achieving accuracy enhancements of 5.49%, 7.38%, 5.79%, and 5.59% on Alexnet, vgg16, resnet50, and resnet101, respectively. Our approach provides technicians with a convenient, intelligent, and precise tool to identify FAW larval instar stages.

articleTitle: Extended-Attention Applied in Selected Stages
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: The Self-attention mechanism was widely applied in Computer Vision (CV) field. However, while Self-attention mechanism brings high accuracy to Transformer, it also brings a huge amount of calculation. To further enhance accuracy and decrease computational load, in this paper, two refinements were implemented. Firstly, two matrices were introduced to enhance the extraction of image information for Extended-attention method. The capacity of Transformer was enhanced by these matrices to capture crucial information in complex tasks, the final accuracy and generalization performance were significantly improved. Secondly, the impact of implementing the aforementioned Self-attention mechanism at various stages of the Transformer is investigated. Intriguingly, our findings reveal that selectively implementing this method at specific stages leads to a significant enhancement in the model's performance.

articleTitle: SED-Net: Speedy Encoding-Decoding Network for Artistic Style Transfer
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: To address the issues of high computational complexity and low adaptability in traditional image style transfer models, this paper proposes a Speedy Encoder-Decoder Network for Style Transfer (SED-Net). This network improves computational efficiency by introducing channel-wise convolution techniques. Additionally, the incorporation of attention mechanisms and Adaptive Instance Normalization between the encoder and decoder enhances the quality and adaptability of style transfer. Experimental results demonstrate that SED-Net achieves efficient real-time transfer and superior performance in terms of SSIM and PSNR compared to traditional Neural Style Transferand Fast Style Transfer. The generated images also exhibit more natural visual effects.

articleTitle: Predicting Accuracy for Quantized Neural Networks: An Attention-Based Approach with Single-Image
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Quantization is an important technique for lightweight deployment of neural network models on resource-limited hardware devices, but current neural network model quantization methods suffer from large loss of accuracy for complex tasks and poor generalisation, which affects the application of deep learning models and large language models in real intelligent scenarios. The root cause of these problems lies in the unclear principle of generating computational accuracy loss in the process of neural network model quantization, and the lack of an effective method for evaluating the quantization performance of the model. To address the above problems, we construct a single-image input accuracy predictor based on the self-attention mechanism, which can quickly predict the computational accuracy of the quantized neural network model by generating a single input image representing the whole test set and the corresponding accuracy predictor through the Transformer encoder and decoder. The method can quickly assess the performance of the model during the model development process, which is conducive to the optimisation of the quantization parameters of the model iterations and promotes the practical application of neural network models.

articleTitle: MF-SPNet: Dilated Convolutional Pyramid with Attention Mechanism for Semantic Segmentation of Street Scenes
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: In the traditional semantic segmentation of street scene, it is difficult to extract target features due to the different sizes of images, the occlusion of targets and the difficulty of recognizing small targets.
