Images are difficult to be semantically segmented efficiently by these models. To solve the above problems, a pyramid network using spatial attention mechanism based on atrous convolutional pyramid (AMF-SPNet) is proposed. Firstly, the feature pyramid fused with dilated convolution is used to extract the features of the target. In the original ASPP model, we change the pooling layer to atrous convolution, and change the interior of the pyramid to atrous convolution with expansion rate 1,3,6,12,18. This model can expand the receptive field of the convolution kernel without increasing the number of parameters. Secondly, the spatial attention mechanism is added to the network, so that the model can better pay attention to the street view target information. Finally, the cityspaces dataset is used for verification, and the MIoU reaches 88.3%, the MAP reaches 89.6%. Compared with other network models, the proposed model can extract the location information and spatial information of street view images more accurately, so that the accuracy of semantic segmentation is improved.

articleTitle: Improved Forest Fire Smoke Image Segmentation Model Based on GVF Model
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: This article proposes an improved fire smoke image segmentation model (UGVFOF) based on the GVF model. The two components of the UGVFOF model and the image gradient are coupled through the use of Laplace operators on the manifold during the generation process. Due to the coupling term taking into account more image information during the diffusion process, UGVFOF snake outperforms traditional image based fire and smoke detection methods in some aspects, such as weak edge protection, target separation, and converging to deeper concave surfaces while retaining certain advantages such as expanding capture range and insensitivity to initialization. The extensive image experiments in this article demonstrate its advantages.

articleTitle: Anti-Occlusion Object Tracking Algorithm Based on Kalman Filter
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: When Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) performs object tracking tasks, it faces problems such as target out-of-view and occlusion, which have a great impact on the tracking performance. In this paper, an anti-occlusion object tracker based on a Kalman filter is proposed, which can effectively deal with the occlusion problem of objects. Firstly, a high confidence measure was proposed to detect tracking anomalies, and Kalman filter was introduced to predict the object motion trajectory and generate object candidate regions. Secondly, the historical target template is used to correlate the target candidate area to obtain the relevance response map, and the target relocation is realized according to the relevance response map. The proposed algorithm is compared with other tracking algorithms on two UAV benchmark datasets, and the results show that the proposed algorithm has better tracking performance.

articleTitle: Application of the MUTAN Model to the VQA Task
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: This research compares Simple-VQA-V2 and Complex-VQA-V2 models in the context of Visual Question Answering (VQA). Simple-VQA-V2 focuses on basic elements and counting, while Complex-VQA-V2 incorporates MLB fusion and Mutan fusion. Both models exhibit similar patterns of accuracy improvement during training, starting with a gradual increase and then reaching a plateau. However, Complex-VQA-V2 demonstrates more variability and lower accuracy compared to Simple-VQA-V2. Surprisingly, the advanced fusion methods do not significantly boost the performance of Complex-VQA-V2. The study underscores the importance of understanding dataset characteristics and making informed choices regarding fusion techniques for multimodal VQA models. It also underscores the potential of Mutan fusion for object counting in images.

articleTitle: A Multi-Objective Intelligent Control Method for Active Distribution Power Network Using Proximal Policy Optimization Agents
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: To effectively mitigate the operational risks of active distribution power grid with growing stochastics and uncertainties caused by renewable generation, this paper proposes a novel multi-objective intelligent control method based on the Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) algorithm for regulating various types of controllers of active distribution network with a high ratio of photovoltaic and power electronics-based devices. The OpenDSS tool is used to model power equipment in distribution networks by incorporating the time-series load patterns, weather index, PV generation profiles for representing realistic operational scenarios. The intelligent control method successfully achieves the objectives of voltage regulation, power loss reduction and minimized control costs. Case studies demonstrate that this method significantly enhances power grid performance, exhibiting adaptability and robustness to changing environmental conditions.

articleTitle: A Physiological Signal Denoising Method Using Adaptive Kalman Filter
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: During the process of physiological signal acquisition, the target signal often encounters various sources of noise interference, including external electromagnetic field interference and internal physiological electrical signal interference, with power line interference being the most severe. These noise interferences pose a significant inconvenience to the analysis and processing of physiological signals. This study proposed a denoising method based on adaptive Kalman filtering, leveraging the advantages of dynamic weight adjustment in adaptive filtering and the state estimation function of Kalman filtering to accurately estimate the signal and noise states, thus eliminating power line interference and other noise interferences mixed into physiological signals. By processing electrocardiogram (ECG) and blink electrooculogram (EOG) collected in a normal experimental environment, the results demonstrate that the adaptive Kalman filter designed in this study can effectively eliminate power line interference and make the target signal clearer and cleaner. The average reduction in spectral amplitude at 50Hz exceeds 52.6 dB. Compared to traditional notch filter processing, this method not only eliminates the fundamental frequency and harmonic components of power line interference but also preserves the useful components of the target signal, providing a more effective solution for the analysis and processing of physiological signals.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Traffic Carbon Emission Prediction Models Based on X-KELM
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Transportation is an important industry for carbon emission reduction, and swarm intelligence technology, as a very important and significant branch of artificial intelligence, is an efficient method for solving complex optimization problems, and shows better performance in the field of carbon emission prediction. In this paper, we use the 2015–2019 Shanghai transportation carbon emission data to do example analysis, and apply Bundle Adjustment (BA), Firefly Algorithm (FA), Cuckoo Search (CS), Grey Wolf Optimizer (GWO) and Whale Optimization Algorithm (WOA) to KELM to establish a transportation prediction carbon emission model. From the data conclusions, it can be seen that the BA-KELM model is more stable, with the lowest coefficient of variation compared to the lowest, with a value of 0.065, and the minimum number of iterations of WOA-KELM is 6 times and the highest model accuracy, with the values of MAE, RMS, MAPE, and R2 of 0.0257, 0.0331, 0.1070, and 0.9686, respectively. it can be seen that from the data conclusions, the WOA -KELM model has high accuracy and fewer iterations in transportation carbon emission prediction, but the stability needs to be improved.

articleTitle: Hybrid GRU-Down-U-Net Deep Learning Model for Breast Invasive Ductal Carcinoma Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Breast cancer(BC) is a type of tumor that start to proliferate in the breast cells and, in recent years, it has gradually become a major issue for women's death. Because the early detection and diagnosis of breast cancer can increase the cure rates, scientists keep finding ways to detect breast cancer earlier. However, the traditional artificial detecting method is a time-consuming task and both its efficiency and precision is relatively low. In order to improve the efficiency and precision, researchers have begun using machine learning models to detect breast cancer and got great results. In our paper, we propose the GRU-Down-U-Net model, which is modified by the GRUU-Net model, for the automatic classification of breast invasive ductal carcinoma(BC-IDC). We trained, validated and tested the model on the dataset, and calculated the accuracy, specificity, sensitivity and F1 score during the testing process to detect the effectiveness of the hybrid model. The results showed that our model performed better than previous models of other researches, which indicates that our model is more robust than previous models during BC classification.

articleTitle: Real-Time Target Detection Method for UAV Embedded Platform
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: With the continuous development of UAV embedded platform in the direction of small size, low power consumption and low cost, the real-time object detection method deployed on it has become a research hotspot in the field of deep learning. Most of the existing mainstream target detection methods are based on large model design, which has the characteristics of complex architecture and huge calculation amount, and the detection accuracy is low when there is similar interference to the target in the UAV aerial image, which is difficult to deploy to the UAV embedded platform to meet the application requirements of real-time accurate detection. In this paper, a real-time object detection method deployed on embedded platform is proposed. Based on the idea of full convolutional architecture, a lightweight model based on twin network is designed, which makes the method have high real-time and detection accuracy. On the self-built ship data set, the detection accuracy can reach 87.35%, and the detection speed can reach 40FPS on the embedded platform, which meets the application requirements of real-time accurate detection.

articleTitle: Robot Visual Inertial SLAM Algorithm Based on Point-Line Features
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: In weakly textured situation, the point feature SLAM system has a large localization error due to the failure to extract enough point features, and even the running trajectory is lost. To address such problems, an improved point-line feature monocular VINS-mono (IPLM-VINS) system is proposed. Line feature information is introduced to the front-end of the system. In order to address the issue of a large number of redundant short lines in the EDlines, we proposed a length suppression strategy. In the back-end sliding window optimization, line feature reprojection error is incorporated. Furthermore, the Huber kernel function is applied to IMU residuals, point-line feature residuals, and loop closure constraints to mitigate the impact of outliers on the optimization results. Comparative experiments were conducted on the public EuRoC dataset, and the positioning accuracy and real-time performance of IPLM-VINS were significantly improved compared to several state-of-the-art VIO systems. The results demonstrate that the positioning accuracy of IPLM-VINS system is improved by 22.9% on average compared with that of VINS-mono. Experiments are carried out in real weakly textured scenes, and the localization accuracy of the improved algorithm is increased by more than 30%.

articleTitle: Wide-area Crop Yield Prediction Based on Multi-Source Remote Sensing Data Fusion and Attention Net
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: The development of remote sensing technology has facilitated the prediction of crop yield over large areas, and more researchers are using multi-spectral geographic data of the growing season to mine the characteristics of crop growth and harvest. However, most of the existing methods do not make full use of dimensionality reduction embedding technology and spatial heterogeneity. In this paper, we use multi-spectral time-series images of crop growth process, combined with non-time-series regional images such as elevation and slope, and learn from better data embedding methods to predict yield by convolutional neural network and self-attention network. We evaluated the method in the county soybean yield forecasting task in the United States, and the experimental results showed the effectiveness of the method.

articleTitle: Gynecological Disease Diagnosis System Based on YOLOv8
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: To meet the needs of image analysis in gynecological laboratory medicine, the traditional gynecological health monitoring methods have encountered bottlenecks and challenges in medical imaging diagnosis. Because traditional methods rely on manual testing and pathological image analysis, requires a lot of time and professional knowledge, so there is a time consuming and subjectivity strong problem, urgent need for more effective solutions. Based on this background, we have adopted advanced deep learning technology, designed and implemented a system that can automatically extract the features, detection, classification and a variety of department of gynecology common pathological image segmentation. The system in experiments showed high accuracy and efficiency, as the doctor provides a rapid and accurate pathological image analysis platform. The findings are expected to provide automation and accurate diagnosis of disease of department of gynaecology important support, promote the improvement of the level of medical diagnosis, treatment effect is of great significance to the improvement of patients.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Data Augmentation Method for Modern Cigarette Packaging Defect Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: This study addresses the issue of insufficient quantity and incomplete types of defect detection datasets for cigarette packages in modern industrial production line scenarios. We propose a cigarette packaging defect data augmentation method. The method consists of three components: preprocessing for obtaining cigarette package defect data through segmentation and cropping based on Segment Anything Model(SAM), generation of cigarette package defects using Cigarette Box Defect-Improved Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Model (CBD-IDDPM), and We expanded the original dataset by utilizing 600 generated images and trained different defect detection models using the augmented dataset. The experimental results validate the effectiveness of our dataset augmentation method for cigarette package defect detection. The mAP50-95 of YOLOv8n has increased from 73% to 75.2%.

articleTitle: A New Algorithm for Path Planning in Dynamic Environments based on Modified Artificial Potential Field Model and Modified Ant-Q Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Artificial potential field and Ant-Q are effective methods for path planning problems. In this paper, several improvements are made for these two methods. First, a new model of repulsive field is proposed to improve the safety of paths. Second, the risk on a path is defined and quantified as a measurement of path quality to further ensure security. Finally, a new algorithm is designed based on these two modified methods. It extends the application field of the ant-Q algorithm to dynamic path planning and meanwhile overcomes the disadvantages of the artificial potential field method. Experiments show that the new algorithm achieved up to an 86% reduction in computational time and a 5.5% reduction in time costs of paths while maintaining safety in environments with dynamic obstacles and targets.

articleTitle: A Survey of Temporal Knowledge Graph Reasoning
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: With the rapid development of science and technology, people use communication, sensor, computer technology and other means to collect, process and analyze information. However, in the era of big data, static knowledge graph technology is difficult to effectively integrate massive amounts of information quickly and in real time. Temporal knowledge graph utilizes timestamp information elements to learn and mine knowledge effectively. Temporal knowledge graph reasoning technology can reason and predict future actions or development trends. This article introduces two ways of temporal knowledge graph reasoning technology, namely temporal knowledge graph reasoning for facial completion and temporal knowledge graph reasoning for prediction, and conducts a comparative analysis. In summary, this article aims to enable readers to deeply understand knowledge graph technology and its application in temporal knowledge graph reasoning, providing valuable references for research and application in related fields.

articleTitle: A Fast Measurement Method of Temperature Field on High Temperature Surface Based on Color CCD
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: The rapid and accurate measurement of high-temperature fields holds significant implications in the realms of aero-engine measurement, metal welding, and the metallurgical industry. This paper proposes a method for rapid temperature field measurement in high-temperature environments, leveraging a color CCD. Initially, we analyze the sources of error in high-temperature measurement scenarios. Subsequently, we design a rapid temperature field measurement method for high-temperature environments using a Multi-layer Perceptron, which includes model construction and dataset creation that takes into account the sources of high-temperature errors. Using the proposed method, we invert the temperature field to obtain visualization data. The efficacy of the temperature field measurement method is validated and tested through high-temperature experiments using a standard blackbody furnace. Experimental results indicate that the proposed temperature measurement method can measure up to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2000^{\circ}C$</tex>, while maintaining a relative low measurement error. This represents a substantial improvement over traditional least squares fitting temperature measurement methods in high-temperature scenarios.

articleTitle: SAR Aircraft Target Detection Based on Improved YOLOv8
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Aiming at the problems of weak generalization ability and poor detection effect caused by strong background interference and small size of aircraft target in SAR (Synthetic Aperture Radar) images, this paper proposes an aircraft target detection algorithm for SAR images based on improved YOLOv8. In view of the shortcomings of YOLOv8 network in small target detection, the Simplified-YOLOv8 network is proposed. Combined with the advantages of DCN (Deformable Convolutional Networks), a C2f_DCNv3 module is proposed to improve the feature extraction ability and anti-interference ability of the model. EMA (Efficient Multi-Scale Attention) is introduced into the neck network, so that the algorithm can retain more feature information in the stage of feature fusion. Inner-CIoU Loss is used as the loss function to improve the convergence speed and regression accuracy. The experimental results on the SAR-AIRcraft-1.0 dataset show that the proposed algorithm achieves a 69.4% reduction in parameter quantity and a 25.9% reduction in computation. The precision rate, recall rate and mAP reach 86.3%, 90.8% and 95.2% respectively. The proposed algorithm greatly reduces the model complexity while ensuring high detection effect. Compared with other popular algorithms, the proposed algorithm is more suitable for aircraft target detection in SAR images.

articleTitle: A Dual Attention Fusion Network for SAR-Optical Land Use Classification Based on Semantic Balance
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: The rapid development of remote sensing technology has enhanced the acquisition of multi-modal data. Optical and synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images, as a uniquely complementary pair, have been proven highly effective in land use classification tasks, allowing for more accurate and detailed analysis of surface characteristics. However, existing approaches often rely on simple fusion methods and ignore the semantic relationships between modalities. Moreover, network models often focus on merging extensive contextual semantic information across channels to capture broader scene features, neglecting the connection between spatial textures and details. To address these issues, the dual attention optical and SAR image fusion network (DAOSNet) is proposed in this paper to balance semantic interactions between modalities and supplement local spatial information. DAOSN et consists of two key modules. Firstly, the dual attention fusion Transformer (DAFT) module can create cross-modal sensory fields to enhance global interactions between pixels in the spatial dimension. Additionally, the modal semantic balance (MSB) loss is introduced to promote deeper semantic collaboration between modalities and preserve the unique perspectives of each modality. The experimental results on the WHU-OPT -SAR dataset demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms other fusion-based approaches, with an improvement of 1.4% in overall accuracy (OA), 10.4% in mean intersection over union (MIoU), and 1.8% in Kappa compared to the MCANet.

articleTitle: Locking Latch Loosening Detection of Train Based on YOLO Framework
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: This study introduces a novel YOLO-based method enhanced with the Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) for detecting loosening in electrical box cover latches, a crucial safety component in train operations. Utilizing a dataset of dynamic train images captured by side-mounted cameras, the proposed two-stage detection process effectively addresses challenges such as small target detection and high background noise. Our findings indicate that CBAM integration significantly improves the model's fault detection capabilities, achieving a recall rate of 0.992 for loosened latches and maintaining perfect precision (0.956) for normal latches, thereby substantially reducing false positives. This approach marks a significant advancement in computer vision applications for railway maintenance, enhancing the safety and reliability of rail transport.

articleTitle: Deep Learning with Gated Recurrent Unit Recurrent Neural Networks and Multi-Objective Optimisation for Portfolio Management
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: A large body of literature to-date suggests Fama and French Five Factor Model (FFFFM) as the “best of regression” algorithms for financial stock return regression. In the present paper, we will study whether the nonlinear regressions like deep learning - Gated Recurrent Unit Recurrent Neural networks (GRU RNNs) and machine learning - Support Vector Regression (SVR) can improve the prediction using Fama and French Five Factors. Our experiments using financial data showed that deep learning - GRU RNNs performed the best among the three models, and the final returns of the Portfolio using optimal weights showed it achieved the best return prediction among them. We proposed a novel portfolio management framework based on stock prediction using GRU RNNs and multi-objective optimisation to help investors to maximize their profit with minimal risk.

Author Keywords: Gated Recurrent Unit Recurrent Neural networks

articleTitle: Dynamic Regulation Domain Adaptation Network for Cross Domain Bearing Fault Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Domain adaptation is an effective approach to address the discrepancies in probability distributions between source and target domains. In this paper, we propose a Dynamic Regulation Domain Adaptation Network (DRDAN), which features a novel feature fusion module within the feature extraction phase. This module not only targeted high-level abstract features but also delved into capturing low-level detailed features. The integration of these two types of features allowed the network to harvest a richer and more comprehensive set of information, thereby providing robust support for the subsequent domain adaptation processes. In the feature alignment phase, DRDAN implemented a dynamic regulation strategy that accounted for both the variances in marginal distributions and the implications of conditional distributions. This facilitated a more precise and adaptable adjustment of feature distributions, ensuring accurate alignment between source and target domains. Our evaluation, conducted using a bearing database as the experimental dataset, affirms that DRDAN significantly bridged the domain gap and enhanced the classification accuracy of data in the target domain.

articleTitle: A Feature Extraction and Detection Method for Multi-Scale Defects on Mineral Surface
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: This study focuses on the practical engineering application of mineral surface defect detection. To address the complexity and large-scale variations of mineral surface defects, we developed a multi-scale mineral surface defect detection model. By refining the Atrous Spatial Pyramid (ASP) and integrating a pre-trained Xception architecture, we effectively extracted and enhanced multi-scale defect features on mineral surfaces. Subsequently, a Feature Pyramid Network (FPN) was utilized to fuse defect features and locate the multi-scale mineral surface defect. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model excels in recognizing multi-scale mineral surface defects, significantly improving the accuracy and efficiency of defect detection.

articleTitle: PE3DNet: A “Pull-Up” Action Quality Assessment Network Based on Fusion of RGB Image Data and Key Point Optical Flow
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: “Pull-up” is a regular physical fitness test in high school and college physical education, and the traditional manual supervised assessment method has the problems of strong subjectivity, large error and low efficiency in the assessment and training of “Pull-up”. In order to solve these problems, this paper proposes an action quality assessment network PE3DNet for “Pull-up” video streams, which uses OpenPifPaf to generate key points, constructs key points optical flow data using key points, and adopts P3D residual blocks to construct a dual-stream network that fuses RGB image data and key point optical flow to achieve the action quality assessment of “Pull-up”. Through the validation experiments on the self-made dataset SKD-PULL, the results show that PE3DNet achieves 92.8% Accuracy, 92.9% Precision, 91.3% Recall, and 92.1% F1 score in the standardized action of “Pull-up”, which effectively improves the accuracy of the action quality assessment of “Pull-up” program and brings higher efficiency and fairness to the sports testing process.

articleTitle: Fast Inter Partitioning of CU Based on Neural Network for Versatile Video Coding
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: The versatile video coding standard (H.266/VVC) is able to save about 50% bit rate on average compared to the previous generation video coding standard H.265, but at the cost of a huge increase in coding complexity. In order to reduce the time consumption of VVC during inter-frame coding, A method based on neural network which does not contain convolutional operations is proposed. The network is trained for 20 sizes and 5 levels of CU using residual image and some temporary variables and the network is invoked during the video encoding process and skip several partitioning modes with lower probability to speed up. The network structure contains only fully connected layers and Leaky ReLU layers, which can fully utilize the CPU performance. Compared to the original scheme, our method saves 60.07% coding time at the cost of 4.41% bitrate in Random Access configuration.

articleTitle: An Improved YOLOv7 Based Concrete Defect Detection Method
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Concrete is widely used in numerous buildings, and timely detection of concrete defects is significant. Currently, the detection of concrete defects mainly relies on manual visual inspection methods. However, manual inspection has many work efficiency, accuracy, and safety issues. In recent years, with the rapid development of computer vision technology, many studies have begun to attempt concrete defect detection methods based on deep learning networks. This paper proposes a concrete defect detection method based on an improved YOLOv7 network, which enhances the detection performance of minor target defects such as cracks by integrating the ACmix attention mechanism and separation-merge operations. To increase the difficulty of defect detection, this paper constructs a concrete defect dataset containing various defect in various environments. The effectiveness of the improved method is verified through ablation experiments, and comparative experiments with Faster R-CNN, YOLOv4, SSD, and other target detection networks which demonstrated the advancement of the enhanced network.

articleTitle: Neural Network-Based Prediction Intervals for Uncertainty Quantification in VI Curves
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: The voltage-current (VI) curve often exhibits uncertainties due to component tolerances and variations in measurement techniques, potentially compromising fault analysis accuracy. This paper proposed a fault analysis approach utilizing neural network-based prediction intervals to quantify uncertainty in circuit board VI curves. Firstly, a neural network is designed to precisely model the VI curves, employing a mean squared error loss function to ensure the model's fidelity in capturing the curves' distinctive features. Secondly, statistical methods are applied to estimate the uncertainty of the modeled VI curves, depicting the fluctuation range of the VI curve. For the fault analysis phase, two critical indicators: coverage rate and curve similarity are incorporated to enhance the fault detection process. Finally, simulation experiments conducted on experimental circuit boards confirm the efficacy of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Safety Helmet Detection Method in Complex Industrial Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Detection of safety helmets is of great significance in the industrial field. In complex industrial scenes, there are environmental problems such as background interference, small targets, occlusion, and poor lighting. At the same time, the real-time nature of the model also needs to be considered. Among existing methods, YOLOV8 has achieved a relative balance in performance and efficiency, but its accuracy in complex scenarios has certain deficiencies. This article proposes a multiview feature pyramid MFP (Multi-granularity Feature Pyramid) network model, which uses three branches to observe objects from different angles for safety helmet detection, and combines it with YOLOV8. This model improves the detection accuracy of safety helmets in complex industrial scenes while maintaining the original advantages of YOLOV8.

articleTitle: SAR Target Detection Based on EfficientDet and Convolutional Block Attention Module
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) has been widely used in military and civilian fields due to its ability to monitor targets all day and all weather. As a key link in the SAR image interpretation, object detection has received widespread attention. In response to the problem of unsatisfactory target detection performance due to the complexity of SAR image scenes, this paper applies the first stage object detector EfficientDet to SAR target detection task and adds the convolutional block attention module (CBAM) in the classification and regression branches. It enables the network to better autonomously learn the useful information and improves the performance of SAR target detection. The experimental results on miniSAR data also verify the effectiveness of the proposed object detection method.

articleTitle: YOLOv9-SAM: A Novel Image Segmentation Method for Industrial Pointer Meter
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: In industrial settings, meters are widely employed for diverse measurement operations. In practice, pointer-style meters are designated for areas with flammable or explosive hazards that require manpower to read the meters. In order to increase the manual efficiency of labor and avoid errors that can result from human interpretation. In this paper, we propose a fuse Segment Anything Model (SAM) with You Only Look Once version 9 (YOLOv9) to resolve industrial pointer meter segmentation. Our method includes two components: (1) we enhance the YOLOv9 with an attention module, which achieves better precision in detecting the point meter. (2) the detection result will be introduced into the prompt module to make the Segment Anything Model focus more on the point meter, meanwhile making the process faster. Our proposed method achieved a detection accuracy of 92.5%, surpassing the original YOLOv9, 87.7%. As for the segmentation part, our method realized a stable, intact dial segment with 90% less operation time. Our enhanced detection and segmentation model has reached a better detection precision and a more accurate segmentation compared to origin methods.

articleTitle: Multi-Scale Mixed Pixel Network for Remote Sensing Image Super-Resolution
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Deep learning-based image super-resolution (SR) technology has gained extensive attention in the remote sensing community, which aims to reconstruct the abundant details of target images. However, the practical application of existing deep learning-based SR methods is often limited by the trade-off between network performance and computational load. This paper presents a novel multi-scale mixed pixel network (MSMP-Net) to explore the precise and cost-effective SR reconstruction of remote sensing images. Specifically, a dual-path feature capture mechanism (DPFCM) architecture is devised that incorporates diverse dilated convolution operations to comprehensively capture hierarchical features across varying receptive fields. In addition, a triple-path high-resolution rebuilder (TPHRR) structure is designed, which uses a set of dense branches, residual branches and pyramid branches to effectively promote the transfer and reuse of features. Extensive experiments reveal that our proposed MSMP-Net outperforms other state-of-the-art SR methods in reconstruction effects.

articleTitle: YUB-200: A Dataset for Fine-Grained Bird Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: The research on fine-grained recognition of bird images has received widespread attention, but currently there are few publicly available datasets of fine-grained bird images, and there are problems such as incomplete annotated data and low image resolution, making it difficult to train deep learning models with high recognition accuracy. Therefore, this article focuses on the research needs of deep learning based fine recognition tasks and constructs a high-resolution bird image dataset. The dataset contains a total of 200 classes of different birds, with 60 images for each class, totaling 12000 bird images. Each image in the dataset provides bird class information, three semantic parts bounding boxes, bird object segmentation masks, as well as the external characteristics, habitat environment, and geographic distribution of each bird class. This dataset was evaluated through fine-grained bird image classification, fine-grained bird image parts detection, and fine-grained bird image segmentation, verifying its effectiveness in fine-grained bird image recognition tasks. In the validation of the classification, the top-1 accuracies of SPDA-CNN, PS-CNN, MASK-CNN, Attention-CNN, Bilinear-CNN, RA-CNN are 90.7%, 81.2%, 91.4%, 83.6%, 89.3% and 91.6%. In the validation of bird parts detection, using three YOLOv5 models, the mAP of bird object are 83.52%, 85.35%, 85.96%, and the mAP of bird's head are 57.4%, 58.71%, 59.53%, and the mAP of bird's torso are 61.27%, 62.05%, 62.83%. In the validation of bird semantic segmentation, using ResNet-50 as a pre-trained encoder, the IoU of U-Net, PSPNet, and DeepLabV3+ is 84.98%, 89.69%, and 89.87%, respectively, verifying the effectiveness of this dataset in fine-grained bird image recognition tasks. The collected bird images and all annotated data involved are open source on the project homepage at https://www.ynbirds.cn/.

articleTitle: A Novel Framework for Reservoir Permeability Prediction Using GPR with Grey Relational Grades and Uncertainty Quantification
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Reservoir permeability prediction is crucial for hydrocarbon exploration and production. Traditional methods have limitations, and Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) offers a powerful alternative. However, GPR can be sensitive to kernel parameters. This paper proposes a novel framework, GPR with Grey Relational Lengthscale Adaptation (GRLA-GPR), that incorporates Grey Relational Grades (GRG) from NMR log data into GPR lengthscale updates to improve permeability prediction with a focus on uncertainty quantification. The framework utilizes a Radial Basis Function (RBF) and Matern kernels' GPR model and calculates GRG to capture relationships between NMR data sequences. The calculated GRG values are then used to update the GPR lengthscale during training. A validation strategy is employed to evaluate the performance. The effectiveness of the framework is assessed using accuracy metrics (mean absolute error, mean squared error and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R^{2})$</tex> and uncertainty quantification metrics (variance and prediction interval normalized average width). The results are compared to a baseline GPR model without GRG-based updates. The proposed framework achieved a better performance in terms of accuracy and uncertainty quantification, providing more reliable permeability estimates for informed decision-making in reservoir characterization.

articleTitle: Aerial3D: Real-word 3D Reconstruction for UAV Images
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Image-based 3D reconstruction constitutes a prominent research topic in the field of computer vision, attracting considerable attention both domestically and internationally. The ubiquity of consumer-level unmanned aerial vehicles (UAV) has endowed us with a wealth of aerial images, fostering the emergence of an abundant source of image data for large-scale outdoor scene 3D reconstruction. This paper focuses on addressing the challenge of large-scale outdoor 3D reconstruction using aerial images. The proposed method, Aerial3D, employs an incremental structure-from-motion method for computing a sparse point cloud model and camera parameters. It further utilizes a multi-view stereo method based on depth map fusion for generating a dense point cloud model. The paper introduces a global view selection method, considering factors such as principal axis angle, image resolution, and timing difference between images, to enhance the accuracy and completeness of the point cloud model. The Floating Scale Surface Reconstruction (FSSR) method is adopted for creating mesh and textured models from the generated dense point clouds. The test results of Aerial3D in various real-world scenarios demonstrate that its performance surpasses that of traditional methods such as MVE and COLMAP.

articleTitle: AVF-Lip: High-Fidelity Talking Face Generation via Audio-Visual Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Talking face generation aims to create realistic facial videos with lips precisely synchronized to the input audio, finding broad applications in human-computer interaction, virtual avatars, and video conferencing. Despite significant advancements in previous works, existing methods continue to face challenges in achieving accurate lip synchronization and high visual quality. To address these challenges, we propose a talking face generation framework named AVF-Lip that supports higher resolution and accurate lip synchronization. Specifically, an audio-visual fusion module (AVFM) is first customized to improve lip synchronization performance, and this is further enhanced by introducing a dynamic and fine-grained face mask. Subsequently, to address the problem of lip distortion in high-resolution facial images, we design a set of loss functions based on face sketches to enhance the generation of the lip areas. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our AVF-Lip outperforms state-of-the-art methods in lip synchronization and delivers competitive visual quality, positioning it as a promising solution for high-resolution and high-fidelity talking face generation. Project page: https://wmd-1.github.io/

articleTitle: VisSpecDic: Visual Analysis of Spectrum Situation Data Based on Density Incremental Clustering
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: The omnipresence of wireless communication highlights the importance of efficient radio spectrum management. Traditional monitoring, based on spectral analysis, is challenged by diverse and fluctuating signal environments. This research introduces the SpecVis system, featuring a Density Incremental Clustering (DIC) algorithm that integrates spectral and signal data for enhanced radio spectrum analysis. The DIC algorithm classifies signal data across frequency and bandwidth grids, using density peaks to identify signal locations and a filtering process to minimize noise interference. It also employs connectivity ratios to discern between fleeting and stable signals. The SpecVis system was evaluated within the FM broadcast band, accurately detecting all authorized signals and offering clear visualizations of signal power and time-frequency dynamics. This system represents a novel approach to real-time spectrum monitoring by combining spectral and signal data analysis. Future enhancements will refine algorithm sensitivity and adapt the system for specific monitoring scenarios.

articleTitle: Research on Adversarial Sample Attack Defense Methods for Speech Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Recently, deep learning has achieved significant success in various fields such as image classification, speech recognition, and natural language understanding. However, the security issues associated with deep learning are becoming increasingly apparent, particularly the challenges posed byad-versarial sample attacks. These attacks, which are both covert and potentially harmful, pose substantial security threats to deep learning models. In response to this, we propose a novel defense method against adversarial sample attacks tailored for speech recognition. This method involves constructing an audio reconstruction model that restores adversarial speech samples back to their normal state. The model incorporates an im-proved Wavenet residual network structure based on dilated convolutions, and utilizes Mel Frequency Cepstral Coefficients to enhance audio reconstruction. Experimental results indicate that the proposed audio reconstruction model exhibits superior reconstruction capabilities, effectively restoring and defending against various adversarial sample attacks.

articleTitle: Self-Supervised Image Denoising with Blind-Spot Network and Residual Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: The utilization of deep learning methods in image denoising has witnessed remarkable growth, primarily due to the training on extensive datasets. However, acquiring vast amounts of clean, uncontaminated images in practical settings is both costly and challenging, thus spurring the rise and evolution of self-supervised deep learning approaches. Within this framework, we have identified two primary challenges: enhancing the efficacy of self-supervised learning and ensuring its adaptability across diverse network architectures. To tackle these issues, we introduce a self-supervised image denoising methodology rooted in the Blind2-Unblind framework. This method mitigates information loss inherent in blind-spot-driven denoising techniques and crafts an efficient denoising network leveraging the U-Net and ResNet architectures. By designing a deeper convolutional network structure and carefully tuning training parameters, we enhance the performance of Blind2Unblind while preventing gradient explosions. Experimental results demonstrate that our proposed method achieves an average improvement of 0.16 dB in Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR) and 0.0022 in Structural Similarity Index (SSIM) compared to the original network, thus validating the robustness of the Blind2Unblind training strategy across various network structures.

articleTitle: SRCT: A Structure Restoration of Complex Table Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Complex tables are widely used in fields such as financial reporting and industrial records. However, existing table structure recognition algorithms perform poorly on tables with complex structures. Existing methods for table structure extraction primarily fall into two categories: rule-based/template-based and deep learning-based methods. The former heavily relies on prior knowledge, while the latter requires extensive training and learning on a large number of complex tables, making it prone to overfitting. These methods are designed to address the challenges of recognizing everyday common tables but have not adequately addressed complex tables. To tackle this issue, we introduce a novel SRCT algorithm for table structure recognition. In the SRCT algorithm, we first conduct standardization processing and introduce algorithms such as PHT and DBSCAN to help establish logical coordinate sets, converting the originally unstructured tables into structured ones for better understanding and management. Then, through reconstruction processing, we build the structural correspondence between logical coordinate sets and physical coordinate sets, restoring the tables to their initial states and generating final physical coordinate sets based on reconstruction optimization formulas. We provide a clear and comprehensive explanation of the algorithm's principles, demonstrating its strong generalization ability in handling complex tables. To advance research on complex tables, we have collected and annotated a dataset called CTable. Preliminary experimental results show that our model performs excellently in complex table recognition tasks, achieving accuracies of 92.8%, 93.5%, and 90.8% on the ICDAR 2019, TableBank, and CTable datasets, respectively.

articleTitle: A Polyp Segmentation Method Combining Cross-Layer Attention and Boundary Refinement
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Accurate segmentation of polyps provides an important basis for detecting and preventing colorectal cancer. However, due to the notable variations in the position, size, and number of polyps across different images, and certain images depict polyps with indistinct boundaries, a higher false negative rate was observed in existing algorithms for colorectal polyp segmentation. In this study, we propose a novel colorectal polyp segmentation algorithm that leverages cross-layer attention and boundary refinement techniques. Firstly, a multi-scale feature enhancement module targeting deep features has been designed to accurately locate polyp targets within deep feature maps. In addition, during the decoding phase, spatial attention is extracted from deep features and utilized to weight shallow features, allowing for a progressive fusion from deep to shallow layers, thereby refining the segmentation instances. Finally, the merged features undergo boundary refinement to produce the segmentation map. We performed comprehensive experiments on five widely utilized public datasets. Our algorithm demonstrates superior capabilities in reducing false negative in challenging polyp images compared to existing mainstream polyp segmentation networks.

articleTitle: Distilled Deep Prediction for Community QA
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Community Question Answer (cQA) platforms such as Reddit, Stack Overflow and Quora are helpful to find relevant and timely information about several issues. They provide users the flexibility of asking open-ended questions to a large audience, and replies to such questions may be useful both to the user and the community. However, sometimes users must scour through countless repetitive questions and unrelated answers on cQA to find accurate and appropriate responses to their inquiries. In this paper, a community question and answer relevancy ranking system has been developed via advanced deep machine-learning technology motivated by the feature learning capacity of deep neural networks. With its ability to accurately retrieve the most relevant answers to a user given a question, our model greatly assists users with much more ease. It shows superior performance over baseline based on extensive offline experiments on two different datasets. One is the Yahoo Answers [1] and another is the COVID-19 Open Research Dataset [2]. Our model significantly improves the accuracy and effectiveness of community-based question and answer platforms. Furthermore, in order to meet much more stringent latency and computation requirements for real-time usage, a much more light-weighted model is needed, for which we applied knowledge distillation and developed a novel pipeline for model compression. Results indicate that our distilled deep learning model can perform as well as the original one since the knowledge from the big model has been successfully transferred. The distilled deep learning model has a significant lift on AUC compared with baseline, however it is only around 16 % of the size of the original heavy one.

articleTitle: AutoCrop: An Automatic Approach to Cropping Panoramic Images
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: During the process of image acquisition, factors such as camera motion and lighting changes often affect the usability and viewing ability of panoramic images, resulting in irregular boundaries in the panoramic images calculated by image stitching algorithms. In response to the above issues, in this paper, we propose an automatic cropping method for panoramic images, called AutoCrop which can crop irregular regions and make the edges of the panoramic images more regular, thereby enhancing the usability and viewing ability of the panoramic images. The core idea of the AutoCrop algorithm is as follows: firstly, calculate the binary image for the input panoramic image; Secondly, calculate the maximum inscribed rectangle contained in the calculated binary image; Then, calculate the region of interest of the panoramic image based on the maximum inscribed rectangle; Finally, build the regular panoramic image by the extracted image information within the region of interest of the input panoramic images. Based on this method, we developed an automatic panoramic image cropping software called AutoCrop, which can crop stitched panoramic images into regular panoramic images. The AutoCrop has been tested on several open-source datasets, and experimental results have all proven the effectiveness of this method.

articleTitle: APT Attack Organization Identification Profiling Based on Big Language Models
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: In this paper, we introduce a novel method for detecting APT (Advanced Persistent Threat) malware and generating organizational profiles by integrating deep learning with a large-scale language model. We address the challenges of gradient explosion and vanishing in traditional grayscale image feature extraction by employing an RGB image-based feature representation, which captures richer texture information and enables deeper mining of APT malware characteristics. Our enhanced convolutional neural network model incorporates the Self-Attention mechanism and Spatial Pyramid Pooling (SPP-net) to effectively handle varying image input sizes, significantly improving model adaptability and accuracy. Experimental results demonstrate that our method not only enhances the detection accuracy of APT malware and its variants but also enables precise tracing of the organization behind the APT attack and identification of specific attack methodologies. The outputs from the deep learning model are further processed by a large-scale language model, which provides detailed analysis and generates comprehensive organizational profiles. Visual analysis of APT threat features underscores the effectiveness of our approach in both malware variant detection and traceability. This method empowers security experts with enhanced detection capabilities and detailed organizational insights, facilitating a more informed and timely response to APT attacks. The findings highlight the importance of integrating deep learning and large-scale language models in advancing cybersecurity, particularly in the context of timely APT detection and defense.

articleTitle: Improved Informer for Pose Prediction of Badminton Sports
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: For badminton sports, the close proximity of the initial sequences of certain movements makes it difficult to predict the subsequent movements of badminton players. In order to solve this problem, we propose a variant of the Transformer architecture based on the self-attention mechanism, which adds a classification module based on Informer model. We also introduce a hyperparameter item to balance prediction loss and classification loss. We use Kinect to collect badminton motion data to build our own dataset for model training. A series of comprehensive experiments have demonstrated that the enhanced Informer exhibits a 4.3% and 2.8% improvement in performance on the NTU and Badminton datasets, respectively.

articleTitle: Multi-Channel Color Space Analysis for Nuclei Segmentation in Histopathology Images
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Nuclei segmentation is essential in various medical analysis applications to assess targeted diseased tissue. In histopathology images, the unsupervised learning method widely used for segmenting cell nuclei is based on processing color histopathology images using standard k-means or fuzzy c-means (FCM) algorithms. Previous studies have explored the significant impact of different color spaces on segmentation results. However, under the background of unsupervised cell nuclei segmentation in histopathology images, a research gap exists concerning the integration of multiple color spaces and the utilization of diverse channel combinations within them. Our study aims to investigate the integration of suitable color spaces for enhancing cell nuclei segmentation results. Specifically, we select two color spaces that demonstrate superior segmentation outcomes. To assess the efficacy of nuclei segmentation, we use one of these color spaces as a reference and randomly combine channels from the other color spaces. Through the exploration of different channel combinations, we can leverage their potential synergistic effects to enhance the segmentation performance. The experimental results indicate that the superior nuclei segmentation result is achieved by combining the entire L*a*b color space with the Cb and Cr channels in the YCbCr color space. This finding emphasizes the advantages of integrating multiple color spaces to improve the segmentation outcomes.

articleTitle: MFAN: Multi-Scale Feature Attention Network for Speech Emotion Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Due to the variability of speech signals and the complexity of human emotions, speech emotion recognition (SER) is an important and challenging task. It is crucial in SER to extract rich emotional information. Some research relies on one type of feature to extract emotional information. However, this approach often fails to capture rich emotional information. Some studies employ multiple types of features. Different features enhance the richness of emotional information, but it may also be affected by redundant information, leading to a decrease in recognition performance. In this paper, we propose a multi-scale feature attention network (MFAN) to address these problems. The model utilizes an utterance-level feature extraction module (UFEM) and a multi-scale feature extraction module (MFEM) to extract emotional information at different scales. In UFEM, a global perspective is being used to extract utterance-level emotional features. In MFEM, a multi-scale feature attention mechanism is introduced to extract emotional information at various scales from a local perspective. The attention mechanism is to enable the model to focus on information relevant to emotion recognition, reducing the impact of redundant information and improving the overall performance of the model. The experimental results on the IEMOCAP, RAVDESS, and EMODB datasets demonstrate that MFAN exhibits excellent performance in the field of speech emotion recognition.

articleTitle: Real-World Super-Resolution via Multi-degradation Based Texture Feature Reconstruction
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: In the field of real-world image super-resolution(SR), collecting paired training data is extremely challenging. As a result, some SR methods are trained on synthetic datasets. But there remains a gap when applied to real-world data. To address this issue, this paper proposes a robust multi-degradation real-world reconstruction method for real-world SR based on a texture degradation reconstruction network. This method cleverly overcomes the inadaptability issue associated with solely using synthetic datasets. Specifically, we first train the encoder, decoder, and the proposed SR network using real data. The encoder learns to extract the genuine texture features of input images through training, while the decoder significantly enhances the model's adaptability by incorporating the multi-degradation information. Then, leveraging the trained encoder, decoder, and real LR data, we retrain the SR network. Through this approach, our method can be trained in the absence of paired data and can improve the SR network's adaptability to LR images with unknown degradation. Experimental results indicate that this method outperforms existing real-world SR methods in generating SR outputs with finer textures.

articleTitle: Graph Neural Network with Adaptive Node-Edge Augmentation Strategies for Imbalanced Node Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Graph neural networks (GNNs) play an increasingly significant role in node classification. Most GNNs have been conducted on balanced datasets. However, real-world graphs often reflect imbalanced distributions, with some classes in the graph having a much larger number of nodes than others, leading to accuracy degradation remarkably when applying GNNs. Although some methods attempt to use the interpolation strategy to improve imbalance node classification, they still lack flexibility. This paper presents a graph neural network with adaptive node-edge augmentation strategies (GraphANAS), effectively promoting the performance of imbalanced node classification. Specifically, all nodes in the target minority class are considered to enhance the diversity of node features. Then, we construct an adaptive node generator using the neural network's learnable ability to adaptively produce new nodes with a more diverse set of features. Further, an adaptive edge generator is devised to discriminate whether there is a connection between two nodes and form the final adjacency matrix of the augmentation graph. Experiments on several datasets reveal that GraphANAS has a significant improvement over baselines. GraphANAS offers a plug-and-play adaptive node-edge augmentation strategy for imbalanced node classification.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Tea Tree Leaf Chlorophyll Content Retrieval Using Multi-Angle Polarized Remote Sensing
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Quantitative delineation of leaf chlorophyll content (LCC) within tea plantations is fundamental for optimized management of cultivation practices. Abundant researches have advanced methods for LCC estimation in tea plants, nevertheless, mechanism and influence of polarization reflection caused by specular reflection to LCC retrieval process were less reported. Thus, the present study leveraged multi-angle polarized remote sensing to delve into polarization reflection modeling and characteristic analysis of tea plant canopy, and its impact on LCC estimation was further explored, utilizing vegetation index methods. Results suggested that Maignan (M) polarization reflection model accurately captured variations of polarized reflectance, RMSE values between simulated polarization reflectance and its measured equivalent within 400–1000 nm spectral domain hovered around 0.0013, under forward observation paradigms encompassing <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0^{\circ}, 10^{\circ}20^{\circ}$</tex>, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$30^{\circ}$</tex>. Specular reflectance component, calculated from polarized reflectance, wielded the most substantial influence on LCC estimations via NDVI in forward <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$30^{\mathrm{o}}\text{observation}$</tex>, compared with backward <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$20^{\circ}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0^{\circ}\text{observations}$</tex>. Separation of specular reflection component rendered a noteworthy enhancement in the inversion accuracies of NDVI model for LCC estimation, approximately by 25% under a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$30^{\circ}$</tex> forward observation condition. The improved model accuracy indicators were quantified as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{R}^{2}= 0.53,\text{RMSE}=12.67\mu \mathrm{g}/\text{cm}^{2}$</tex>, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{RPD} =1.45$</tex>, highlighting the criticality of specifying and adjusting for specular reflection components in the enhancement of LCC estimation models using NDVI methods.

articleTitle: Blended Latent Diffusion Under Attention Control for Real-World Video Editing
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Due to lack of fully publicly available text-to-video models, current video editing methods tend to build on pretrained text-to-image generation models, however, they still face grand challenges in dealing with the local editing of video with temporal information. First, although existing methods attempt to focus on local area editing by a predefined mask, the preservation of the outside-area background is non-ideal due to the spatially entire generation of each frame. In addition, specially providing a mask by user is an additional costly undertaking, so an autonomous masking strategy integrated into the editing process is desirable. Last but not least, image-level pretrained model hasn't learned temporal information across frames of a video which is vital for expressing the motion and dynamics. In this paper, we propose to adapt a image-level blended latent diffusion model to perform local video editing tasks. Specifically, we leverage DDIM inversion to acquire the latents as background latents instead of the randomly noised ones to better preserve the background information of the input video. We further introduce an autonomous mask manufacture mechanism derived from cross-attention maps in diffusion steps. Finally, we enhance the temporal consistency across video frames by transforming the self-attention blocks of U-Net into temporal-spatial blocks. Through extensive experiments, our proposed approach demonstrates effectiveness in different real-world video editing tasks.

articleTitle: Quantization Technology for Neural Network Models with Complex Branching Structures
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Model quantization is one of the means to address the difficulty of deploying models in resource-constrained environments. A quantization framework for integer-only inference across the entire network can better compress the resources required for computation and enhance the efficiency of model computation. Unlike mainstream model quantization frameworks that quantize by inserting quantization nodes into convolutional layers or fully connected layers, integer-only inference quantizes all operators in the model, including pooling and activation functions. However, in the case of multiple branches, there is a strong dependency relationship between the quantization parameters of model operators. Therefore, resolving the conflict of quantization parameters in complex branching structures is key to ensuring the accuracy of the quantization in the integer-only inference framework. This paper proposes a quantization technology for neural network models with complex branching structures, which resolves the conflict of quantization parameters in complex branching structures based on the topological relationships of the computation graph. This technology achieves a quantization loss of no more than 4% across models with different tasks and bit widths, demonstrating the effectiveness and practicality of this method.

articleTitle: Aberrant Brain Structure-Function Decoupling in Generalized Epilepsy Revealed by Graph Signal Processing
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Genetic generalized epilepsy is a neurological disorder associated with multiscale alterations in brain network organizations. However, the epilepsy-related brain structural-functional interaction abnormalities remain largely unknown. Here, we applied graph signal processing to estimate regional structure-function decoupling (SFD), which described the decoupling strength between brain functional activity and underlying anatomical architecture. We investigated brain SFD alterations in 86 patients with genetic generalized epilepsy with generalized tonic-clonic seizures (GGE-GTCS), and 114 healthy controls. Relative to control subjects, individuals with GGE-GTCS revealed SFD decreased in occipital, parietal, and superior temporal cortices, whereas SFD increased in frontal, cingulate, and inferior temporal cortices and subcortical nucleus accumbens and caudate areas. The SFD alteration pattern was spatially correlated with gamma-aminobutyric acid neurotransmitter density. Collectively, our findings provide insights on clarifying brain structural-functional reorganization in GGE-GTCS.

articleTitle: Leather Defect Detection Algorithm Based on an Improved YOLOv5s
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: In the field of intelligent manufacturing, the realization of efficient and accurate automated surface defect detection is particularly critical for enhancing product quality, especially in the leather industry, which holds a significant position in global trade. Traditional defect detection methods encounter challenges in handling complex scenes and identifying minute defects. However, the advent of deep learning technologies has provided a new pathway to address these issues. This paper is dedicated to innovative research on the precise localization and detailed classification of leather surface defects through the enhancement of deep learning models, aiming to overcome the limitations of existing technologies and improve the accuracy and efficiency of detection. By extending the YOLOv5s model, this study has developed the CMR-YOLO algorithm. This algorithm integrates the Channel Attention mechanism (CA), an improved Multi-Dimensional Precision Intersection over Union (MPDIoU), and the Cross Stage Partial Residual feature enhancement module (C3R). These enhancements not only improve the classification accuracy but also bolster the model's stability and robustness in complex scenes. Through the comprehensive application of these techniques, the CMR-YOLO algorithm demonstrates improved performance in categorizing different types of leather defects, particularly effective in handling diverse defect characteristics and accurately classifying various defects. Compared to the traditional YOLOv5s, the CMR-YOLO algorithm also exhibits improved accuracy in defect classification, with the mAP50 increasing from 62.5% to 79.5%, effectively enhancing the overall performance of leather defect detection. These research outcomes not only achieve technological breakthroughs but also provide significant technical support for quality control and intelligent manufacturing in the leather goods industry.

articleTitle: Precise Image Editing with Multimodal Agents
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: The rapid advancements in large language models (LLMs) have revolutionized the field of artificial intelligence, enabling the development of sophisticated agents capable of performing complex tasks. The emergence of multimodal LLMs, such as GPT-4 Vision, has further expanded the possibilities by allowing agents to process and understand visual data directly. However, current end-to-end solutions for image content editing often fall short in terms of stability, precision, and interpretability. Motivated by these limitations, we propose a novel framework that leverages the capabilities of multimodal agents to execute precise image editing tasks in a sequential and logical manner. Our approach integrates a comprehensive suite of advanced image editing tools into the action space of the agent, enabling it to interact directly with these tools through their APIs. Additionally, we introduce a reflection mechanism that empowers the agent to critically assess its own editing output and refine its actions accordingly. Through extensive experimental validation across diverse image editing scenarios, we demonstrate the effectiveness and superiority of our approach over existing end-to-end methodologies. Our contributions include the development of a versatile and flexible multimodal agent framework for image editing, the establishment of a new benchmark for precision and reliability in AI-driven image editing, and the laying of groundwork for future research in the integration of cognitive capabilities and visual perception in AI.

articleTitle: Leaf Chlorophyll Content Retrieval from Hyperspectral Measurement Using Convolutional Neural Network and Continuous Wavelet Transform Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Dynamic monitoring chlorophyll variations is imperative for overseeing crop growth dynamics and biophysical exchanges. Previous studies have established methods for leaf chlorophyll content assessment using hyperspectral reflectance. Compared with traditional remotely sensing methods, convolutional neural network (CNN) excels in representation learning ability, while continuous wavelet transform (CWT) has the capacity to unveil nuanced spectral changes. Nevertheless, integrative studies employing both CWT characteristics and CNNs within the context of leaf chlorophyll content (LCC) assessment were rarely reported. Aiming at this problem, the present study harnessed abundant leaf data, namely ANGERS, NEON, and winter wheat, to investigate the capability of synthesizing AlexNet and CWT features for LCC assessment. Results revealed that AlexNet model informed by CWT features, at 21 decomposition scale, best captured LCC variations, achieving an R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> of 0.98, an RMSE of 3.52 μg/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, an RRMSE of 11.00 %, and an RPD of 6.41. Further validation confirmed an increment in R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> by 0.19, a reduction in RMSE by 2.83 μg/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, and a 7.70 % reduction in RRMSE for LCC estimates when compared with results using raw spectral reflectance. These findings corroborated the substantial potential CWT holds in conjunction with AlexNet for robust LCC estimation, advocating for increased integration of these methodologies in remote sensing assessments of crop physiological parameters.

articleTitle: SAFE-MVS: Multi-View Stereo Based on Self-Attention and Feature Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Deep learning-based Multi-View Stereo (MVS) stands as a significant area of focus in computer research, to reconstruct 3D point cloud models from multi-view images. However, current MVS methods have not fully capitalized on global and local information within the feature extraction network, particularly in occluded and shadowed regions, where these approaches struggle to extract adequate image features. To tackle these challenges, this paper proposes a multi-view stereo method named SAFE-MVS based on self-attention mechanisms and feature enhancement. The core idea of this method is twofold. Firstly, it integrates self-attention mechanisms into the feature pyramid network to autonomously learn features from previous stages, thus enhancing the robustness of image features. Secondly, we incorporate a feature enhancement module into the cost volume construction stage. This module expands the receptive field of convolutional layers and incorporates positional information into the extracted features, thereby improving the model's generalization capabilities in extensive scenes. Subsequently, this paper evaluates the proposed MVS method on the DTU dataset and compares its performance against existing classical MVS methods. The experimental findings demonstrate that the proposed MVS method outperforms classical MVS methods, significantly enhancing the accuracy and completeness of point cloud models. Moreover, experimental results demonstrate that the SAFE-MVS method reconstructs point cloud models with more complete and comprehensive edges compared to the CVP-MVSNet and Cas-MVSNet methods. Additionally, the SAFE-MVS method surpasses both CVP-MVSNet and Cas-MVSNet in terms of accuracy.

articleTitle: Ensembling Lightweight Models for Intelligent Waste Recognition Based on Degraded Images
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Traditional waste recycling predominantly depended on labor-intensive manual waste classification, a solution that neither efficient nor time-saving.
