In a bid to enhance the efficacy of recycling, relevant researchers incorporate computer vision and deep learning methodologies to facilitate rapid waste sorting. However, existing waste recognition models can not effectively recognize waste based on degraded images, nor can they be flexibly applied to different application platforms. Consequently, we introduce an intelligent approach grounded in ensemble learning for waste recognition in intricate scenarios. Initially, we construct a new waste image degradation dataset and simulate waste recycling scenarios under different illumination and motion conditions using synthetic degradation methods. Subsequently, we investigate various image recognition networks and ensemble learning methods for waste recognition, and introduce a novel query ensemble learning approach aimed at striking an optimal equilibrium between model parameters and recognition accuracy. Furthermore, we conduct relevant comparative analyses to substantiate the advantages of our methodology. The empirical outcomes indicate that our solution outperforms other deep learning models and achieves satisfactory results for accurate waste recognition based on degraded images.

articleTitle: Hybrid Attention Mechanisms and Bio-Inspired Optimization for Enhanced Breast Cancer Diagnosis from Ultrasound Images
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Breast cancer is one of the most prevalent cancers worldwide. Early detection through medical imaging screening and timely diagnosis are crucial for improving prognosis. How-ever, interpretation of complex ultrasound scans is an arduous task even for experienced radiologists. Computer-aided diagnosis (CADx) systems can aid clinicians by automatically analyzing images to identify malignant cases. This research presents a novel deep learning framework with hybrid attention mechanisms and bio-inspired optimization (HAM-BIO) to enhance ultrasound-based breast cancer diagnosis. Custom residual blocks equipped with multi-level attention modules help selectively focus on discriminative imaging attributes indicative of tumors. Grey Wolf Optimization adaptively evolves model hyperparameters for superior topology and convergence. Evaluations on two breast ultrasound datasets achieve state-of-the-art classification accuracy, 96.7% on dataset 1 and 88.9% on dataset 2, sur-passing existing CADx systems. The models optimization and interpretability enhancements improve automated breast cancer screening without additional data. These results highlight the techniques clinical utility and potential. By integrating compu-tational intelligence and explainable AI, the approach sets new standards for supporting radiologists with accurate diagnostic assistance.

articleTitle: FF-UNET: An Enhanced Framework for Improved Segmentation of Brain Tumors in MRI Images
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: With the development of medical imaging technology, accurate and effective tumor segmentation is crucial. In this study, we investigated the potential of deep learning based brain tumor MRI image segmentation technology. We propose an enhancement method called FF-UNET, which utilizes feature fusion and combines the capabilities of UNet and CNN models to improve segmentation accuracy. Using preprocessing techniques to improve tumor visibility, and then using a customized layered UNet model for segmentation. To reduce overfitting, a discard layer is introduced after each convolutional block stack. In addition, the CNN process utilizes the context of brain tumor MRI images to further enhance the segmentation performance of the model. In two datasets, our method achieved an accuracy of over 98%, with accuracy and Jaccard coefficients exceeding 90%. The experimental results indicate that our proposed framework outperforms state-of-the-art models in distinguishing brain tissue. The FF-UNET model has great potential as a feasible diagnostic tool, enabling radiologists to accurately segment brain tumor images and improve patient care.

articleTitle: Structural Prior Knowledge Integrated Deep Learning Method for Tiny Object Identification
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: With the rapid development of energy, manufacturing, and other industries, there has been a significant increase in the demand for equipment monitoring and maintenance. Taking an optical modem as an example, the connection status of the device can be monitored by analyzing its indicator labels and lights. However, detecting these indicators poses challenges due to their small size and potential interference. To achieve automatic equipment monitoring and enhance equipment maintenance efficiency, we propose a cascaded knowledge-integrated object detection method that leverages the inherent structural characteristics of the equipment. We focus on the detection region within the entire image and identify the object in this specific area. This approach effectively mitigates noise interference, enhancing both efficiency and accuracy in identifying regions of interest. Our method demonstrates strong scalability, making it suitable for status detection across various communication equipment. We evaluated our proposed method using datasets collected from real-world scenarios, ultimately achieving an impressive accuracy rate of 97.7%.

articleTitle: A Memory Management Method for DNN Inference for Aerospace Embedded Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Currently, deep neural networks(DNN) are widely used in aerospace field, however, due to the embedded system in aerospace field, it is often difficult to support large-scale in-orbit inference calculation of deep neural networks due to the resource constraints in memory and power consumption. In order to effectively reduce the memory space occupied by deep neural networks during inference computation, we propose a memory management method for deep neural network inference computation by establishing a two-dimensional model of size and lifetime for memory allocation, and by fusing three strategies of time-first, size-first, and area-first in the consideration of both depth traversal and breadth traversal of the computational graph. In order to reduce the memory consumption of intermediate computation results by deep neural networks during inference computation, we determine the optimal memory reuse scheme between different intermediate computation result tensors by arranging the intermediate computation result tensors in the two-dimensional plane without overlapping. We also tested typical deep neural network algorithms based on the self-developed TIANJI NPU, and the test results show that our method has achieved a large improvement compared with the original method of TIANJI NPU software toolchain, and the maximum reduction in memory usage reaches 85.51%, and the minimum reduction is 21.31%.

articleTitle: A Method of Rolling Bearing Fault Diagnosis Using Transfer Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Rolling bearing fault diagnosis is an important task that is critical for realizing predictive maintenance in industry 4.0. However, due to the lack of labeled data of rolling bearing faults and the complexity of working conditions, it is expected to construct fault diagnosis model with good generalization through leveraging a small number of labeled data collected from limited source domains and make it perform fault diagnosis well in other target domains. In this paper, we propose a method of rolling bearing fault diagnosis using transfer learning. We first construct a group of Domain-Adversarial Neural Networks (DANNs), each of them does its best to identify the faults of target domain via making the distribution of each source domain data and the distribution of the target domain data become similar as much as possible. After that, the group of DANNs are combined through the Mixture of Experts (MoE) to build the fault diagnosis model MoE-DANN, which achieves satisfactory fault diagnosis results in the target domain by unleashing the potential and balancing the effect of each expert. Extensive experiments demonstrate that MoE-DANN yields better diagnosis accuracy on open benchmark datasets than the baseline models. Additionally, it generalizes well even it is trained by a limited number of labeled data.

articleTitle: Remote Sensing Based Advance Image Captioning Improved Feature Attention
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: In the domain of image description generation, the focal point mechanism is crucial for highlighting the most relevant features within an image, thereby influencing the quality of generated descriptions. To address this challenge, we introduce an innovative optimization module called the Enhanced Focal (EF) mechanism, which builds upon the traditional multi-head focal point mechanism. The EF module is designed to assess the correlation levels between objects within an image, thereby guiding the process of subtitle generation more effectively. The EF mechanism integrates the output of the multi-head focal point mechanism with the current context (i.e., the query) to generate two components: an “information vector” and an “attention gate.” The “attention gate” is then applied to the “information vector” to create a refined focal point mechanism. This refined mechanism undergoes element-wise multiplication with the “information vector,” producing attention information that reveals a strong correlation between the target and the background in the image. This process leverages the Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) mechanism to enhance the model's capability to capture intricate relationships. Upon training and evaluating our enhanced model on the MS COCO dataset, we observed significant improvements in key evaluation metrics. The BLEU-1 and METEOR scores reached 73.01% and 28.81%, respectively, showcasing the effectiveness of the proposed EF mechanism in improving image description generation.

articleTitle: Study on Large-Scale Crop Disease Epidemic Forecasting Based on a Fusion Model Between SEIR and LSTM Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Establishing effective models for dynamically forecasting crop diseases is crucial for supporting grain production in China. Addressing the challenge of fusing the mechanistic model and multi-sources data, this paper proposes the SEIR-LSTM model, which integrates the SEIR mechanistic model with Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network. The SEIR model captures disease trends based on biological mechanisms, while LSTM models nonlinearly represent multiple driving factors, achieving high-precision dynamic disease forecasting. The model is validated across counties in Hunan Province, China. Experimental results demonstrate that the integrated SEIR-LSTM model effectively captures disease trends and nonlinear patterns between driving factors and disease epidemic. In cross-county forecasting, the average RMSE is 4.716, the average MAE is 4.116, and the average r is 0.706, indicating high forecasting accuracy and regional generalization. This model can provide effective decision-making support for crop management practices.

articleTitle: Mamba-Based Residual Network for Remote Sensing Image Super-Resolution
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Image super-resolution is the process of recovering high-resolution images from low-resolution inputs, which is crucial in low-level computer vision tasks. In recent years, progress in deep learning has significantly propelled the development of image super-resolution technology. Various models, such as convolutional neural networks (CNNs), generative adversarial networks, Transformers, and diffusion models, have been employed to address this problem with significant impact. Among these models, CNNs are effective in capturing local features but have limitations in modeling long-range dependencies; Transformers, despite their powerful modeling capabilities, face computational bottlenecks due to the quadratic complexity of the self-attention mechanism when dealing with large images. To address these issues, we propose the Residual Mamba Block, which combines state space models (SSMs) with residual connections, providing a linear complexity attention mechanism that effectively enhances long-range dependency modeling. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness and superior performance of the proposed method. Furthermore, our research indicates that vision state space models have great potential to become a foundational framework for future super-resolution tasks.

articleTitle: Image Reconstruction Leveraging Time-Event Feature Fusion for Event Cameras
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: The event cameras generate asynchronous event sequences, rendering most existing image-based algorithms in-applicable for direct use and processing. Therefore, the development of a simulator that utilizes event streams captured by an event camera as input and reconstructs image sequences as output is crucial for subsequent tasks such as high-speed moving object tracking, object recognition and detection, and SLAM. Despite the extensive research and attention garnered by deep learning-based image sequence generation, there remains a problem of local representation information loss during the reconstruction process from event streams to image sequences. Existing solutions, whether based on Stacking Based on Time (SBT) or Stacking Based on Events (SBE), exhibit significant limitations when using a single stacking approach. To address the insufficiency in feature representation capability, this paper proposes a visual image conversion method based on multi-view feature fusion, effectively transforming event streams into traditional image sequences. Extensive experiments and dataset validations, utilizing multiple evaluation metrics including both global and local assessments, demonstrate the advantages of our proposed method.

articleTitle: Research on Ship Fault Identification Based on Optimized Convolutional Neural Network Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: The identification of abnormal vibration noise of underwater ships is of great significance for troubleshooting ship faults to prevent damage deterioration and ensure its vitality. Aiming at the problems of many parameters and low recognition efficiency of existing intelligent diagnostic models, an underwater ship abnormal vibration noise fault identification method based on convolutional neural network is proposed, which optimizes the traditional neural network (BP), enhances the nonlinear expression ability of the convolutional neural network model by introducing convolutional kernel; and replaces the fully connected layer in the traditional convolutional neural (CNN) network with the average pooling layer to reduce the model parameters and computation amount while preventing the overfitting phenomenon. parameters and computation amount, while preventing overfitting phenomenon. The abnormal vibration noise of underwater ships is tested using the rolling bearing vibration noise dataset for alternative experiments to verify the feasibility of the method. The experimental results show that the method can accurately identify different fault states and is faster and more accurate than the traditional intelligent diagnostic model, which has certain potential for practical engineering applications.

articleTitle: Improved Conditional Posterior Cramér-Rao Lower Bound for Geometry-Dependent Bistatic Radar Measurement Uncertainty
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Recently, the conditional posterior Cramér-Rao lower bound (CPCRLB) is proposed by incorporating sensor acquired target's historical measurements into its recursion derivation, and provides an online bound to evaluate the lowest mean square error (MSE) an estimator can achieve in theory more faithfully. Whereas, the existing CPCRLB completely neglects the fact that radar measurement uncertainty is significantly dependent on the target-to-radar (T2R) geometry, and discards available target information that unavoidably results in bound deterioration. Motivated by the fact that radar measurement uncertainty is significantly dependent on the T2R geometry, this paper formulates the geometry-dependent target measurement uncertainty model for bistatic radar system and derives an improved CPCRLB (ICPCRLB) with imperfect detection based on this model. Because of fully accounting for the impact of geometry-dependent target measurement uncertainty on the conditional bound, the proposed ICPCRLB is a more accurate MSE bound than the existing CPCRLB. Simulation results demonstrate the superiority of the proposed ICPCRLB over existing state-of-the-art bounds.

articleTitle: LEGO Minifigure Recognition Based on Deep Learing
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: LEGO® is a building block company that allows children and adults to create endlessly changing shapes through brainstorming. It is so admired that people call it “Magic Plastic Building Blocks”. Exquisite LEGO Minifigure of various themes also increase the fun of Lego bricks. This paper uses deep learning methods to predict and recognize LEGO Minifigures. This paper employs four different convolutional neural network models for training. Due to the tiny dataset size, the experimental results were suboptimal. To address this issue, transfer learning is introduced to mitigate the overfitting problem. Additionally, three different optimizers are utilized to conduct the final evaluation of the model's performance. After applying the transfer learning method, the experimental results show that using the VGG 16 model with an RMSProp optimizer has the best performance.

articleTitle: CSA-LSTF: An Improved Method for Time Series Data Anomaly Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: With the development of industrial Internet of Things (IoT), a large number of sensors have been deployed in practical environments to collect data. These data possess characteristics such as large volume, high dimensionality, strong time series nature, and high real-time requirements, making anomaly detection difficult. Traditional anomaly detection mainly focuses on single data streams, which leads to high model maintenance costs and an inability to determine dependencies be-tween multidimensional time series data, thus failing to meet the practical requirements of current industrial IoT scenarios. This paper proposes an improved algorithm CSA-LSTF(Convolutional Sparse Self Attention-Long Sequence Time-Series Forecasting) based on LSTF, which utilizes convolutional sparse self-attention mechanism to enhance LSTF and applies this algorithm to the framework of Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) for training. Anomalies are detected through discrimination results and reconstruction errors. Experimental results demonstrate that the CSA-LSTF method can timely detect anomalies and take preventive measures, enhancing the risk resistance capability of industrial IoT systems. Compared with existing anomaly detection models, it enhances model stability, improves anomaly detection accuracy, and surpasses existing multidimensional un-supervised time series data anomaly detection models.

articleTitle: Recommendations for Healthcare: An Interpretable Approach Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: This study introduces a novel approach to patient interpretation and diagnosis, utilizing Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) within a collaborative recommendation framework. Our proposed system employs GNN-based collaborative filtering to model complex patient-patient and patient-symptom relationships in a comprehensive graph structure. The system is designed to offer interpretable recommendations, explaining the reasoning behind diagnostic suggestions. The study focused on common chronic conditions in older adults, including high blood pressure, coronary heart disease, diabetes and stroke, as well as fractures, osteoporosis and arthritis. We used a graphical hybrid recommender system (GHRS) and a cooperative graph neural network (GCFNA and GCFYA) to predict hospital disease diagnosis. Encouragingly, both the GCFNA and GCFYA models achieved prediction accuracy rates of over 90%, highlighting the model's excellent performance in accurate predictions. The ultimate goal is to provide precise disease predictions for elderly patients, offer medical guidance, and enhance patient care in hospitals, particularly in managing chronic diseases.

articleTitle: Data Augmentation in Medical Materials Science: A Review
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: With the rapid development of computing methods, traditional methods of medical materials science analysis are unable to keep pace with today's development, especially when multiple chemical factors are contributing at the same time. Most artificial intelligence (AI) techniques in medical materials science are based on traditional machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL). Nonetheless, the two methods are limited by the amount of data. Thus, data augmentation (DA) was introduced to medical materials science to solve this problem. This paper aims to provide an overview of DA applications in medical materials science. A general procedure is stated. Crucial scientific guidance for future innovations in medical materials science based on DA is also presented.

articleTitle: A Novel Spatio-Temporal Information Knowledge Distillation Strategy for Weak-Supervised Video Anomaly Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Video anomaly detection (VAD) is highly valuable for applications in intelligent monitoring systems. However, due to the complexity of video, as well as the lack of detailed annotation information, VAD remains a challenging problem. Although existing self-training-based methods make process in anomaly localization and reduce the need for annotation information, they still suffer from two limitations: 1) insufficient spatio-temporal information correlation in two-stage model; 2) ignoring label noise. To address the above issues, we propose a novel self-training video anomaly detection framework based on spatio-temporal information knowledge distillation (STKD-SVAD). Specifically, we design a spatio-temporal information knowledge distillation strategy to establish correlations for spatial and temporal information. Furthermore, we design a temporal information module (TIM) and a spatial information module (SIM) to enhance the temporal and spatial information, respectively. Moreover, we add multi-instance loss in the second-stage of self-training framework to reduce the interference of label noise. Experimental results on public datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our method.

articleTitle: An Improved Merge-YOLOv5 Algorithm Applied to Helmet Wear Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Safety management is a vital link in site operation, and wearing a safety helmet is crucial in protecting workers' heads in the construction environment. However, some site operators need more safety awareness, and accidents caused by not wearing safety helmets often occur. Therefore, it is of great significance to monitor the wearing of safety helmets. This paper attempts to improve the traditional target detection algorithm YOLOv5 by updating the NMS function in the original algorithm, which improves the recognition accuracy of the algorithm by making the prediction frame more accurate. After the improvement, compared with the original YOLOv5, the performance indexes of Soft-YOLOv5, Ciou-YOLOv5, Diou-YOLOv5, Giou-YOLOv5, and Merge-YOLOv5 are improved. The mAP@0.5:0.95 performance indexes of Merge-YOLOv5, Soft-YOLOv5, Ciou-YOLOv5, Diou-YOLOv5, and Giou-YOLOv5 increased by 3.0%, -1.4%, 2.5%, 2.3%, and 2.4% compared with original YOLOv5. The results show that the improved performance of Merge-YOLOv5 is outstanding, and it is more suitable for the on-site inspection of safety helmets.

articleTitle: MAML-TSC: Model-Agnostic Meta-Learning for Time Series Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: User portrait technology, involves analyzing historical usage records of household electronic devices, is evolving quickly. Traditional methods using LSTM or CNN for time series classification face challenges in achieving high accuracy with limited data. To address this, our study introduces MAML-TSC, which combines a dual-channel Transformer with model-agnostic meta-learning (MAML). This model features a dual-channel Transformer that leverages a multi-head self-attention mechanism to extract information from both time and channel axes effectively. By incorporating MAML, the model harnesses knowledge transfer to optimize initialization parameters for diverse training tasks, enhancing performance with fewer data samples. Experimental outcomes show MAML-TSC achieving 90% accuracy in the meta-learning phase and maintaining over 80% after 10 iterations, outperforming the DeepConvLSTM baseline by 12.5% and surpassing most current deep-learning approaches.

articleTitle: AIGLLM: An Action Instruction Generation Method with Visually Enhanced LLM
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Action Instruction Generation (AIG) is a key step in semantic-driven action sequence generation, which aims to embed text instructions describing specific actions into the driving text. AIG is a challenging task that requires accurately understanding the potential action semantics contained in the driving text. Besides, the challenge is exacerbated by the lack of paired text-action instructions data. To address these challenges and motivated by the powerful capabilities of LLMs in text generation, we propose AIGLLM, a novel AIG framework with visually enhanced Large Language Model (LLM). Specifically, we perform low-rank adaptation (LoRA) on the off-the-shelf LLM to enable the model understand action semantics and generate action instructions at appropriate positions within the original text sequence. Particularly, to address the current lack of data that can be used to fine-tune LLMs for AIG, we construct a dataset containing 12,000 text-action instruction pairs and 15,000 image-action instruction pairs. Subsequently, a visual module is designed to enable the LLM to learn action knowledge from external visual signals of actions, thereby enhancing the model's understanding of action semantics. Finally, we conduct extensive experiments, where the experimental results and evaluations demonstrate that our method has an impressive key benefit: improved accurate action instruction embedding.

articleTitle: TransSnake: Contour-Based Wild Animal Instance Segmentation Using Contour Transformer
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Wild animal instance segmentation technology plays a significant role in wild animal research, enabling automatic wild animal information extraction, improving data processing speed, and reducing researcher burden. Inspired by the Snake algorithm and Transformer, we propose TransSnake, a new contour-based instance segmentation model. Its process included three stages: initial contour, coarse contour, and refined contour. In the coarse contour stage, we introduce a multi-scale fusion module to fuse multi-scale contour information, expand the receptive field, and generate a higher-quality coarse contour. The obtained coarse contour lays a solid foundation for subsequent contour refinement. However, relying solely on local information for contour deformation can result in substantial prediction errors. Therefore, we adopt the contour transformer in the refined contour stage to capture global information among contour points. This module uses global information to guide contour deformation and improve segmentation accuracy. Experimental results illustrate the outstanding performance of our method on the LoTE-Animal dataset and validate the feasibility of contour-based instance segmentation methods in wild animal segmentation. Meanwhile, the excellent performance is also shown from our approach on the SBD dataset.

articleTitle: MSFF: A Novel Multi-Modal Semantic Feature Fusion for Social Media Fake News Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Social media has become the primary channel for spreading fake news content, and the form of fake news is gradually evolving from a single form to multi-modal forms including text, voice, images and videos etc. This paper proposes a novel multi-modal semantic feature fusion (MSFF) for social media fake news detection based on text semantics and visual entity representation methods. Through this method the text and image unimodal features are first classified and extracted, Next the BERT language model is utilized for text features and VGG19 convolutional neural network utilized for image features to vectorize representation. Then the multi-modal features are merged and they are mapped into semantic consistency feature labels through the attention network. Finally weighted joint detection results for fake news are reached. Experimental validation conducted on PolitiFact and GossipCop in the fake news detection dataset FakeNewsNet demonstrates that the MSFF model increases the accuracy rate and recall rate by 2.6% and 5.6% respectively compared to the current state-of-the-art methods, which indicates that the method can fully integrate multi-modal feature information and effectively enhance the performance of detecting fake content in social media news.

articleTitle: Neural Numerical Estimation of Liquid Volume in Transparent Containers via a Single RGB-D Image
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Measuring liquid volume can be perilous and in-efficient under some circumstances. To address this problem, we present a new approach to measuring liquid volume in transparent containers from a single RGB-D image. We propose a novel 10-bit binary encoding of the volumetric value with a corresponding numerical binary-code cross-entropy loss function, i.e., NBCCE loss. We achieve better volumetric prediction than previous methods. Then, We construct a fully convolutional anchor-free volumetric prediction network and embed NBCCE loss into this network. To verify our method, we build an RGB-D image dataset of transparent containers filled with varying amounts of liquid. In experiments, we incorporate our binary encoding and NBCCE loss into a group of classical network structures. Our method results in significantly lower estimation error than L1, smooth L1 or MSE with direct floating number encoding, and the fine-grained classification [1], [2]. Furthermore, our method also outperforms the existing fluid volume estimation method using the equivalent dataset.

articleTitle: Dynamic Low-Rank Adaptation Based Pruning Algorithm for Large Language Models
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Deep neural networks have been getting better and better performance while the parameter size has become larger and larger, and have now entered the era of large language models (LLM). However, large language models with huge number of parameters are difficult to be deployed on edge devices with limited computing power and memory resources. Network pruning techniques can reduce the storage and computation requirements of large language models. Although Dynamic Low-Rank Adaptation (DyLoRA) allows efficient fine-tuning of LLM, the deployment of LLM is still hindered by large model sizes and computational costs. In this paper, we propose a DyLoRA-based pruning algorithm that uses gradient updating of DyLoRA module to define the importance of parameters, and then prune the least important parameters based on the resulting importance scores. Through experiments on commonly used evaluation datasets, it is demonstrated that the proposed pruning algorithm is able to achieve 96.60% of the performance of the original model with 20% of the parameters pruned, which outperforms the previous pruning algorithms.

articleTitle: Alleviating Action Hallucination for LLM-based Embodied Agents via Inner and Outer Alignment
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated impressive potential in empowering embodied agents, fortifying them with task planning and reasoning capabilities closely akin to humans. However, there remain significant challenges in aligning LLM-based embodied agent actions with the executable and safe action space to reduce hallucination. In this paper, we propose a flexible and resource-efficient framework for aligning the action space of LLM-based embodied agents. The framework employs a parameter-efficient fine-tuning method for inner alignment and a retrieval-based generation approach for outer alignment. Specifically, when the inner aligned model generates an action, the outer alignment employs ROUGE to calculate the similarity between the action and all actions within a safe and valid action space, ultimately selecting the action with the highest similarity as the output. For situations with multiple alternative actions, the outer alignment introduces a policy model, which could be either open-source small LLMs or commercial LLMs, to determine the optimal action based on the current context of the agent's task execution. The retrieval-based outer alignment ensures all actions align with an executable action space, alleviating action hallucination for LLM-based agents and significantly improving the controllability and interpretability of their decision-making process. Through extensive experimentation with the LlaMA-2, Bloomz, and OPT models on the ALFWorld benchmark, we validate the effectiveness and adaptability of our framework.

articleTitle: Functional Movement Screen (FMS) Computerized Automated Scoring Technology Research
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Functional Movement Screen (FMS) is an evaluation system widely utilized in various fields such as physical therapy, rehabilitation, physical fitness training, and sports education. Its objective is to assess the performance of individuals in areas such as movement control, balance, and agility. FMS has been extensively employed, requiring substantial manpower. This study is grounded in the FMS scoring criteria and employs the Azure Kinect depth camera to capture three-dimensional skeletal sequence data of the test subject's movements. Through a fully automated process, FMS scoring is initially conducted. Within this automated process, manifold learning algorithms and the dynamic time warping (DTW) algorithm are applied to recognize key frames. The implementation of this approach establishes an automated scoring system for FMS, offering insights for the advancement of human posture assessment systems rooted in functional movements. This contributes to the widespread application of FMS systems.

articleTitle: Lightweight Remote Sensing Object Detection Model Based on Spiking Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Remote sensing target detection harnesses aerial and satellite imagery to drive critical insights for environmental monitoring, disaster response, and strategic planning. However, the successful implementation of high-performance remote sensing object detection currently relies on artificial neural networks, which need substantial computational resources, posing significant challenges for edge computing scenarios. In this study, we capitalize on the energy efficiency of spiking neural networks to design an innovative remote-sensing object detection model. Compared to equivalent ANN models, our model reduces computational resource requirements significantly. Furthermore, to minimize memory requirements, we introduce a dual quantization strategy for membrane potentials and synaptic weights. It quantifies both membrane potentials and synaptic weights to lower bit levels. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our lightweight remote sensing object detection model achieves competitive accuracy on the NWPU VHR-10 and SSDD datasets with an 80% reduction in memory requirements, respectively. Our solution provides a consistently effective strategy on edge devices with limited resources.

articleTitle: A Study of a Sobel Edge Detection and SVM Based ALPR System on an ARM Single-Board Microcomputer
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: License plate is the unique identification of the vehicle, and Automatic license plate recognition (ALPR) systems have emerged as one of the distinctive applications of Image Processing, representing a typical paradigm of optical character recognition (OCR). However, traditional license plate number recognition systems often encounter challenges such as high costs, large sizes, inefficient CPU resource utilization on computer platforms. Utilizing a single-board computer can effectively address these issues, offering more efficient resource utilization and satisfactory task completion. The Linux-based Acorn RISC Machine (ARM) embedded single-board system emerges as a suitable platform for this purpose. This paper primarily investigates an ALPR system based on the open-source image processing library Open Computer Vision (OpenCV), adapted for deployment on an ARM single-board microcomputer, referred to as the ARM-ALPR system in this study. The research encompasses license plate image preprocessing, character segmentation, character recognition, and cross-platform system migration, etc. The proposed methodology employs the Sobel edge detection algorithm and morphological algorithms to delineate license plate outlines, projection techniques for character segmentation, and employs a “one-to-many” recognition approach within the Support Vector Machine (SVM) classifier to enhance accuracy. Additionally, to improve system operability and aesthetics, PyQt5 is employed to design the GUI interface. Finally, the programming code is ported to the Raspberry Pi to realize the license plate recognition system. The Raspberry Pi-based license plate recognition system exhibits cross-platform compatibility and easy portability, capable of running on different hardware platforms with high flexibility and scalability. Therefore, the outcomes of the implementation yield accurate results, indicating its promising potential for a broader range of applications.

articleTitle: SPECTER: A Tracker with Super-Resolution Siamese Network Reconstruction and Multi-Scale Feature Extraction for Thermal Infrared Pedestrian Tracking
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Existing thermal infrared (TIR) trackers attempt to acquire robust discriminative features of the target, as TIR tracking traditionally relies on learning an appearance model of the target. However, the challenge of low-resolution and sparse details in TIR images limits the effectiveness of existing trackers. To tackle this limitation, we introduce a novel tracker for robust TIR pedestrian tracking. Our proposed tracker emphasizes enhancing target discriminability through multi-scale deep feature extraction and high-resolution reconstruction. Firstly, the multi-scale feature extraction and fusion network captures diverse features using a multi-branch structure and incorporates grouped convolutions to extract varied deep features by increasing the cardinality of each group. Secondly, a super-resolution Siamese network is designed with a chain-like structure of stacked feature extraction functions. The core of this network is a Siamese residual block, which progressively aggregates image features through residual learning, extracting deep abstract feature information and improving model generalization. Moreover, by utilizing sub-pixel convolutional layers to reconstruct deep features, high-resolution TIR images are generated to improve target recognition. To the best of our knowledge, we are the first to perform super-resolution technology for TIR target tracking. Extensive experiment results on four TIR tracking benchmarks including LSOTB-TIR, PTB-TIR, VOT-TIR2015, and VOT-TIR 2017 demonstrate that our tracker achieves the best performance compared to other state-of-the-art trackers.

articleTitle: Aerial Target Intention Recognition Based on Deep Belief Network
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: In view of the current complex battlefield data, this paper studies the objects and elements of tactical intention recognition in order to obtain the characteristics of typical aerial target. On this basis, a method for recognizing tactical intentions of aerial targets is constructed. Considering the difficulty of identifying with traditional expert knowledge and experience which is prone to different understandings, a deep belief network is used to recognize tactical intentions based on data learning and probabilistic reasoning methods. By introducing time factor, the proposed dynamic Bayesian network gives the process of event reasoning more continuity to get in line with reality. A genetic algorithm is used to obtain the Bayesian network structure based on a simulated data set, and then the Bayesian network is used for intention reasoning. Finally, a simulation test environment is built and a digital simulation is conducted to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: 3D Abdominal Multi-Organ Segmentation Based on Mamba and Channel-Spatial Cross Attention
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Due to the complexity of the multi-organ structures presented in three-dimensional abdominal medical images, the varying tissue mediums, and the blurred edges, there is a need to construct a segmentation network capable of capturing long-range dependencies and global context awareness to enhance its segmentation accuracy. Traditional convolutional neural network architectures are limited by their receptive fields, the self-attention layers in Transformer are not scalable, and U-shaped segmentation networks often overlook the conceptual discrepancies between the encoder and decoder. Therefore, this paper proposes a 3D abdominal multi-organ segmentation network with Mamba and channel-spatial cross attention. The encoder and decoder stages utilize the DGFN-Mamba module to effectively capture long-distance dependencies and localized details, fully understanding the volumetric context of medical images. Enhancing the global context by employing 3D Channel-Spatial Cross Attention to grasp the dependencies of channel and spatial relationships within multi-scale encoder features. The skip connections have been improved to achieve a comprehensive fusion of global deep semantic and local shallow semantic information during the decoding process. Experimental results indicate that compared with other mainstream 3D medical image segmentation methods, our method shows an increase of 1.78% in the average DSC and 1.56% in the average NSD on the Abdomen CT dataset, compared to the U-MambaEnc method. On the Abdomen MRI dataset, our method shows an improvement of 3.37% in average DSC and 3.39% in average NSD over the nnU-Net method, thereby demonstrating the effectiveness and practicality of our approach.

articleTitle: A Hypergraph Transformer With Adaptive EdgeConv for Skeleton-based Action Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Skeleton-based action recognition is a crucial task in computer vision, aiming to perform pattern recognition on a skeleton sequence to identify the actions represented by the skeleton's semantics. However, current mainstream skeleton-based methods primarily rely on global edge information. Unimportant edges may influence this approach, limiting the model's performance in action recognition tasks. Additionally, because these methods treat all information equally, they may lead to resource wastage. This paper proposes a Hypergraph Transformer-based action recognition method using Adaptive EdgeConv Module(AEM) to address these issues effectively. In this method, we introduce Adaptive Edge Graph Convolution Networks(AEGCNs), which utilize the AEM to adaptive obtain edge sets and edge set weights, thereby adaptive identifying key edge sets. With this information, the model can dynamically adjust the importance of different edge sets based on various samples. This approach improves the accuracy of action recognition and reduces the loss of computational resources. Our experimental results on two challenging benchmark datasets (i.e., NTU RGB+D and NTU RGB+D 120) show that the proposed method is comparable to state-of-the-art methods.

articleTitle: Multi-Task Breast Ultrasound Image Classification and Segmentation Using Swin Transformer and VMamba Models
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Breast cancer represents a significant women's health issue worldwide. Ultrasound imaging is a critical technique for early detection. Additionally, AI-based methods are proving to be crucial. This research compares deep learning methods such as VGG-16, ResNet-50, Swin Transformer, and VMamba in classifying breast ultrasound images as benign or malignant and for segmentation tasks. Notably, this research is the pioneer in utilizing the VMamba model for both the classification and segmentation of breast ultrasound images. Additionally, we have developed a multi-task learning framework that simultaneously produces classification and segmentation results compatible with all underlying networks. This work is a notable advancement in the application of AI within medical imaging, highlighting its potential in early cancer diagnosis and advocating for a combined approach to improve outcomes. We benchmark four existing deep learning techniques in breast ultrasound image analysis and multi-task learning. Our code is available at https://github.com/kuanhuang0624/buscseg.

articleTitle: PC-CSP: An Efficient Partial Convolution in Cross Stage Partial Network for Small Targets Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: The common approach for small object detection does not work well in complex scenes with objects of multiple sizes. This is because the detection of small objects and objects of other sizes often difficult to take into account at the same time. To overcome these limitations, we introduce an efficient Partial Convolution in Cross Stage Partial (PC-CSP) network for detecting small targets. First, the introduction of the DCNv3 module improves the feature extraction for detection, slimneck is utilized to enhance the attention mechanism suitable for objects of varying sizes. Then, PC-CSP is employed to streamline the detection backbone network. Last, the loss function is refined by incorporating the concept of Inner. Through extensive experiments, our method demonstrates a significant increase in accuracy of 6.8%, and mAP@0.5 by 8.97% on the standard dataset compared to the original model. Overall, the proposed method exhibits excellent performance for small objects, such as: mobile phones, food, and faces.

articleTitle: Robust Stereo Matching Using Noise Feature Extraction Network with Dynamic Convolution
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Stereo matching in noisy scenes presents significant challenges, as interference noise blurs the image, leading to ambiguities in matching. Most existing methods attempt to denoise the images prior to performing stereo matching. However, these approaches are not ideal for stereo matching, as denoising algorithms may not only eliminate noise but also valuable texture information, consequently causing matching errors. Furthermore, previous methods struggle to utilize depth cues from the noise effectively, leading to inefficient cost aggregation during stereo matching. To address these issues, we introduce a noise feature extraction network with dynamic convolution (NFENDC) that can extract depth cues from noisy images and improve stereo matching using these cues. In addition, we devise a noise volume representation to systematically capture these depth cues from the noise and fuse it with the cost volume for improved cost aggregation, rectifying the ambiguous matching caused by noise. Experimental results on KITTI benchmarks substantiate that our proposed method significantly enhances the matching performance of state-of-the-art algorithms in noisy scenes.

articleTitle: IVDETR: A Multi-Source Image Pig Detection Method Based on Cross-Domain Feature Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: In large-scale centralised pig farming, object detection algorithms can accurately track and monitor each pig. However, a significant proportion of current detection methods are based on visible images, and the colour differences between different pig breeds limit the applicability of the models. Furthermore, complex background interference, low illumination conditions, or high illumination intensity noise in visible scenes can likewise lead to reduced accuracy during detection. Therefore, we propose a cross-domain encoder based on the self-attention and design the IVDETR model, which integrates features from infrared and visible light images for pig object detection. In order to facilitate the training and evaluation of the model, we constructed a comprehensive, standardised infrared-visible light dataset for the first time. The experimental outcomes demonstrated that the detection accuracy was increased from 0.939 to 0.998 in a real pig breeding environment.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Method of SVG Parameter Calibration Based on Particle Swarm Optimization and Soft Actor-Critic
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Static var generators (SVGS) are essential for compensating reactive power and maintaining bus voltage levels before and after large disturbances. Accurate modeling of SVG controller parameters is critical to ensure the reliability of dynamic simulation in power system operation. This paper introduces a novel SVG parameter identification method, which integrates the benefits of particle swarm optimization (PSO) and reinforcement learning (RL) to improve the efficiency and accuracy of parameter calibration. We use simulation data generated by PSD BPA software combined with actual power grid data as the environment to optimize the parameter settings of SVG. This study combined PSO with the Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) algorithm to optimize and calibrate these parameters. Compared with the simulation results, our method shows significant advantages in calibration accuracy and processing speed and effectively improves the simulation quality and practicability of the SVG model.

articleTitle: Cross-Modal Contrastive Learning for Robust Reasoning in VQA
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Multi-modal reasoning in visual question answering (VQA) has witnessed rapid progress recently. However, most reasoning models heavily rely on shortcuts learned from training data, which prevents their usage in challenging real-world scenarios. In this paper, we propose a simple but effective cross-modal contrastive learning strategy to get rid of the shortcut reasoning caused by imbalanced annotations and improve the overall performance. Different from existing contrastive learning with complex negative categories on coarse (Image, Question, Answer) triplet level, we leverage the correspondences between the language and image modalities to perform finer-grained cross-modal contrastive learning. We treat each Question-Answer (QA) pair as a whole, and differentiate between images that conform with it and those against it. To alleviate the issue of sampling bias, we further build connected graphs among images. For each positive pair, we regard the images from different graphs as negative samples and deduct the version of multi-positive contrastive learning. To our best knowledge, it is the first paper that reveals a general contrastive learning strategy without delicate hand-craft rules can contribute to robust VQA reasoning. Experiments on several mainstream VQA datasets demonstrate our superiority compared to the state of the arts.

articleTitle: Study on Multi-channel Color CCD-based Temperature Measurement for High-temperature Objects
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: This paper proposes a temperature measurement method for high-temperature object surfaces using a color CCD camera. This method leverages the multi-channel photoelectric conversion principle of the color CCD camera to achieve efficient and real-time temperature detection of high-temperature objects. Moreover, when faced with a large temperature measurement range or high-temperature objects of varying temperatures, the temperature measurement approach based on the radiometric colorimetry of the CCD sensing elements exhibits varying degrees of applicability. This paper discusses the differences between varIOUs channel-based colorimetric temperature measurement methods and their applicable objects. Specifically, the selection and analysis of two-channel and three-channel methods are presented.

articleTitle: AutoFill: An Automatic Approach to Filling Panoramic Images
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Panoramic image filling stands as one of the foremost research topics in the field of image editing. The purpose of image stitching is to repair the blank area at the edge of the panoramic image, ensuring alignment with the original scene, and enhancing overall quality and usability. This paper proposes an efficient and high-precision automatic approach (called AutoFill) for filling panoramic images to defend the issue that missing edge information in panoramic images. The AutoFill method comprises the following key steps: first, calculate the binary image (Mask) for the input panoramic image; second, based on the binary image, calculate the area of the panoramic image that needs to be repaired; third, extract of pixel information from the neighborhood area surrounding the blank region to be repaired; and finally, use the extracted pixels to fill the blank area to produce the high-quality panoramic image. Multiple open-source data sets were used to evaluate the proposed AutoFill, and experimental results demonstrated its efficiency. Our method successfully completes the panoramic image filling task.

articleTitle: LSTDNet: A Long-Range Spatio-Temporal Decoupling Network for Traffic Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Traffic flow forecasting is integral to the functionality of intelligent transportation systems, with the primary challenge lying in the accurate representation of intricate spatio-temporal relationships. However, few existing models address two key problems: how to accurately capture long-range spatial correlations and how to learn from the long-term spatio-temporal context. To address this, we propose a Long-range Spatio-Temporal Decoupling Network (LSTDNet) for traffic prediction. Briefly, LSTDNet uses two masking autoencoders in the pre-training phase to mask and reconstruct traffic flow sequences along the temporal and spatial axes, respectively, in order to capture long-range spatial-temporal correlations from long-term spatio-temporal contexts. Then, the learned spatio-temporal embeddings are fed into a multilayer network in the prediction phase to obtain the final prediction results. Experiments on four publicly available real-world datasets show that LSTDNet can effectively capture long-range spatio-temporal correlations and achieve competitive results.

articleTitle: Electronic System Integration Technology for Intelligent Missile Weapons
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Aiming at the development trend of intelligent missile weapons, this paper analyzes and summarizes the four intelligent characteristics of missile weapons, proposes an integrated design method of electronic system for intelligent missile weapons, and discusses the hardware architecture, software architecture and communication architecture of the system. The functions of the intelligent integrated information processing system are abstracted and mapped to several functional modules. The hardware architecture adopts the mode of passive backplane plus functional modules based on VNX standard, the software architecture adopts the mode of open multi-level operating system plus application software, and the communication architecture adopts the low, medium and high-speed hybrid bus structure. An intelligent, integrated and modular platform architecture that can realize missile autonomous decision-making, information fusion, intelligent killing and cooperative operation is built. Finally, the key technologies required for the integrated architecture of intelligent missile weapon electronic system are discussed and its feasibility is analyzed.

articleTitle: Deep Neural Network Accelerator: Exploring the Potential of 3D Chiplet Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: The development of deep neuro networks brings a sharp rise in demands for expeditious convolutional computing operations, but the “memory wall” originated from the intense data transfer, has greatly hindered the performance of deep neural network accelerators. As the integrated circuits have entered the post-Moore's law era, evolving the neural network accelerator by advance semiconductor fabrication technology is no longer available. This paper presents an in-depth analysis of data flow within a fundamental neural processing unit system, examining the impact of 3D integration and chiplet architecture on overcoming the “memory wall” challenge. A versatile neural processing unit architecture, featuring adjustable processing elements and buffer sizes, is developed to evaluate performance improvements induced by 3D chiplet integration. The results prove the feasibility of 3D chiplet integration in performance advancement of neural processing unit from both memory and processing element perspectives, which provides a complete guidance for potential solutions for reducing memory bottlenecks.

articleTitle: Survey on Ethical Challenges of Implementing AI in Healthcare
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: In today's world, Artificial Intelligence (AI) and its usage concerning human tasks have become an integral part of our daily lives. Humans depend upon AI to provide faster and more efficient solutions. In the world of medicine, where every decision made by a doctor, physician, or consultant directly impacts the lives of those being treated or diagnosed, AI is making its way to help efficiently provide such results as the intelligence of a human being. Healthcare systems around the world are now making use of AI to help provide humane solutions using algorithms and Machine Learning (ML). Fallacies or inaccuracies in the arena of healthcare can have horrendous outcomes for the patient on whom the procedure is being carried out. Sometimes, certain ethics could be traded off by the system, such as confidentiality, autonomy, justice, and biased decisions leading to false results and victim blaming, which directs the masses into not trusting AI-related healthcare solutions. This situation can lead to mishaps like “AI winter,” where the public could start disbelieving the results of AI solutions. This survey review makes an effort to analyze and address these pertinent ethical issues underlying the requirement for algorithmic translucency, concealment, and safeguarding the interests of all those involved.

articleTitle: A Novel Classification Model Based on DWT and CNN-LSTM Motor EEG Imagination Signals
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Feature extraction and pattern classification play important roles in brain-computer interface (BCI) systems, which are widely used in rehabilitation medicine, artificial intelligence and other fields. Although advanced EEG acquisition technology can generate a large amount of EEG data for different brain regions, it inevitably has disadvantages such as high cost, long time consuming and inherent high false positives. Considering the contradiction between data volume and accuracy, this paper proposes a MI EEG feature extraction and classification method based on discrete wavelet transform (DWT) and Convolutional Neural Network-Long Short Term Memory (CNN-LSTM). Based on the project BCI motor imagination EEG(MI-EGG) data set, all evaluation indexes of the proposed CNN-LSTM model are superior to other models. The prediction accuracy, precision, recall rate, F1-score and MCC of C3 and C4 channels reaches 96.43%, 96.57%, 96.57%, 96.57% and 93.02%, respectively. The reliability of the proposed model is also proved by tenfold cross-validation. The average accuracy is 99.64%, which is far higher than the other models. It can be concluded that it is a reliable method to predict MI-EEG signals by using CNN-LSTM to train the modeling ability of images.

articleTitle: Overview of Underwater Object Detection Based on Image Processing Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: underwater object detection and recognition are critical technologies in marine science and engineering, enabling advancements in environmental monitoring, resource exploration, and autonomous underwater vehicles. The rapid progression of computing power, underwater robotics, and artificial intelligence has driven substantial academic and industrial interest in this domain. This paper presents a comprehensive overview of the current methodologies in image-based underwater object recognition, where optical images or videos captured under various lighting conditions are processed to detect and identify underwater objects. The discussion includes an analysis of the prevailing algorithms, a review of the contemporary research landscape, and an exploration of emerging trends. Additionally, this paper offers insights into the anticipated technological advancements that will shape the future of underwater object recognition.

articleTitle: Research on Pothole Road Detection and Recognition Based on PyTorch and Improved YOLOv5
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Potholes on road surfaces are one of the pressing issues in urban road maintenance. They not only damage the stability and efficiency of vehicles but also pose a potential threat to the safety of pedestrians and passengers. In view of the limitations of YOLOv5 in feature representation, adaptability to complex scenes, and utilization efficiency of computational resources, this study introduces the CBAM (Convolutional Block Attention Module) attention mechanism into its backbone network. By combining channel attention and spatial attention, the model is able to focus more accurately on the key regions in the image, thereby optimizing feature representation. The improved network model is implemented using the deep learning framework PyTorch, and the model is quantitatively evaluated using metrics such as mAP (mean Average Precision). Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model exhibits excellent performance in terms of detection accuracy and efficiency, which is of significant importance for research and applications in fields such as geological exploration, space science, and natural disasters.

articleTitle: LightGBM Prediction Algorithm Based on Bayesian Optimization and Its Application
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Under the background of the era of artificial intelligence, predicting product demand through machine learning can effectively improve the production and sales benefits of enterprises. Based on the shipment data of a large domestic manufacturing enterprise for dealers, this paper predicts the order quantity of products. Firstly, 597465 data from 1753 products are preprocessed and feature extracted, and 25 features including is _ holiday, Season _ 0, price _ bins, item _ code _ mean _ encoded, sales _chan_name are determined. The LightGBM algorithm is established to predict the product demand in the next three months, and the parameters of min _ child _ weight, lambda _ 12, feature _ fraction, bagging _ fraction, learning _ rate, seed, num _ iterations in LightGBM are optimized by Bayesian algorithm. According to the monthly grain size prediction, R2 is 0.92; Finally, the algorithm is compared. The prediction of BP neural network shows that R2 is 0.70. The experimental results show that the optimized LightGBM prediction result is significantly better than the BP neural network. The algorithm provides a scientific reference for the prediction of product order quantity.

articleTitle: Human Activity Recognition with Dual-Stream Residual Network based on Wearable Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Human activity recognition (HAR) is utilized to monitor human postures and actions in various fields such as human-computer interaction, motion detection and analysis, and medical rehabilitation. Currently, there is a growing interest in human activity recognition using wearable devices. Traditional convolutional neural networks (CNNs) typically use one-dimensional convolution for time-series signals, which makes it difficult to fully exploit high-dimensional features. This paper proposes a dual-stream residual network model for human activity recognition based on Gramian Angular Field (GAF). GAF converts a one-dimensional time-series signal into a two-dimensional image, enabling better observation of weak amplitude changes in the signal and providing better interpretability than traditional conversion algorithms. The experimental com-parison between the proposed model and several mainstream depth models on a local dataset shows that the proposed model outperforms all other models in all evaluation indicators.

articleTitle: ISTAD: Scaled Transformer with Interactive Learning for Multivariate Time Series Anomaly Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Anomaly detection of multivariate time series is of great significance in establishing an efficient anomaly detection system. However, the current research does not take into account the characteristics of different time scales, namely, short-term mode and long-term patterns. This paper proposes a method based on Interactive Scaled-Transformer Anomaly Detection (ISTAD) to solve the above problems. The main idea is to cross the original data sequence to obtain two sub-sequences, and then learn feature sharing in the interactive learning structure. At the same time, the scaled transformer module is embedded to extract the long-term correlation of the time sequence interactively. In addition, the Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) is introduced to capture the short-term correlation of the time sequence. In terms of model design, a joint optimization strategy based on a forecasting-based model and a reconstruction-based model is adopted, and the fusion of single timestamp prediction and reconstruction of the entire time sequence represent information sequences. We conducted experimental verification on the widely used benchmark datasets, and the results showed that our method was better than other methods and reached the most advanced performance level.

articleTitle: A Regression Analysis and Prediction Method for Assembly Error of Aviation Product Components
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: There are many factors that would affect the assembly error in aircraft assembly process, and the coupling rules are complex among those factors. The existing numerical methods cannot effectively analyze the assembly error, resulting in poor assembly accuracy and long development cycle. This paper aims at the small sample size of aircraft assembly site data. By measuring and analyzing the data on the assembly sites, the error modeling method and information feedback mode based on assembly site data were established. On this basis, an assembly tolerance prediction method based on artificial intelligence is proposed. Then, taking typical aircraft parts assembly as an example, the error prediction results of the proposed method in this paper and the traditional neural network method were compared. The prediction accuracy of this paper's method (0.003 mm) is obviously higher than that of the latter (0.011 mm), which verifies the effectiveness and reliability of the proposed method. Finally, the predicted assembly error probability was used to guide the adjustment of the assembly tolerance scheme, thereby improving the assembly accuracy and shortening the assembly cycle.

articleTitle: An Improved YOLOv8 Algorithm for Rotating Object Detection in Unmanned Aerial Vehicle Remote Sensing Images
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicle remote sensing images suffer from problems such as arbitrary object orientation and dense arrangement of small targets, which makes horizontal box object detection difficult. To address these issues, an improved YOLOv8 based remote sensing image rotating object detection algorithm (R-YOLOv8) is proposed. Firstly, the long edge definition method of the five-parameter method is used to represent the rotation box, which allows the bounding box to cover the small target at any angle. This can better fit the actual shape and arrangement of the target, which effectively solves the problem of accidental deletion caused by inaccurate horizontal box positioning. Then, ProbIOU Loss is introduced as the regression loss function to convert the rotation box into a two-dimensional Gaussian distribution, which solves the problem of angle periodicity caused by the representation of rotating targets. Finally, the BiFormer attention mechanism is introduced to improve the accuracy of target detection while reducing parameters and computational complexity. This paper conducts relevant experiments on the UAV-ROD dataset. Compared to classical networks and existing oriented object detection networks, the R-YOLOv8 algorithm performs better in the case of a model size of only 2.8 MB, mAP@0.5 reaches 98.7%, which verifies the effectiveness and progressiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Improving Prediction Accuracy of Bridge Element Deterioration for Decision Support
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Deterministic models can aid decision-making in the maintenance, repair, and rehabilitation of bridges. However, they are often static and exhibit a memory-less property, thereby failing to account for the dynamic or chronic characteristics of bridges. This study established a robust framework for a bridge maintenance model grounded in deterioration curves of individual elements and the corresponding element-level inspection data sourced from the National Bridge Inventory. Specifically, we identified influential variables through a comprehensive literature review and laid the foundation for subsequent analysis. Then, we employed a comparative analysis of machine learning and deep learning algorithms facilitated feature extraction and pattern recognition, with model performance assessed through the accuracies of the Decision Tree (69.50%), XGBoost (63.5%), Random Forest (69.3%), Logistic Regression (71.0%), and ANN (68.34%) models. The resultant methodology exhibited enhanced predictive accuracy for bridge deterioration, substantiated by the scrutiny of model predictions against real-world outcomes. Notably, the Logistic Regression model coupled with Dempster Shafer Theory algorithms demonstrated the highest accuracy, attaining a commendable 71.0% and the capability to achieve the data fusion of micro electromechanical systems, sensor technologies, and historic datasets. Validation tests conducted on the resulting deterioration curves underscored their efficacy in empowering transportation agencies to make informed decisions. By advancing the precision of bridge deterioration prediction, this research seeks to furnish decision-makers with invaluable support in optimizing infrastructure management strategies.

articleTitle: CFGNet: Coarse-to-Fine Grained Network for Image Classification of Confusing Fly Species
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: In the realm of fine-grained image classification (FGIC), despite substantial technological advancements, models frequently misclassify certain fly species with exceedingly high inter-class similarity, thereby impacting overall classification accuracy. To address this challenge, we propose an innovative Coarse-to-Fine Grained Network Framework (CFGNet). This architecture tackles the issue through two stages: Initially, to alleviate classification complexity, closely related and easily confused categories are amalgamated. Subsequently, a lightweight coarse-grained information extraction network (CM) is introduced to enhance the classification accuracy of samples with relatively larger class differences. In the second stage, for precise identification of challenging samples, a fine-grained feature extraction network (FM) is proposed exclusively for difficult-to-distinguish images. Additionally, we introduce a novel feature reuse method to deeply mine and repurpose coarse-grained features from the previous stage to guide fine-grained classification and improve performance in this stage. To validate our approach, we curated a dataset based on merged confusion classes annotation (Flies-MCC). Experimental results demonstrate that our proposed network architecture achieves significant advancements in fine-grained fly classification and offers a pioneering solution for precise fly identification.

articleTitle: EM-YOLO: An Improved Steel Surface Defect Detection Model Based on YOLOv8n
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: The detection of surface defects in steel is vital for guaranteeing the material's performance and service life. However, the actual detection process often encounters challenges such as severe background interference from defective parts and significant variations in defect scales. To address these issues, this paper proposes an improved YOLOv8n model named EM-YOLO. Firstly, to tackle the issue of high background interference, the study designs the ECCA (Enhanced Channel Coordinate Attention) module based on Coordinate Attention, which enhances the capture of channel features and strengthens their interaction with spatial information, significantly improving the model's ability to focus on key features and suppress irrelevant information.Next, to address the multi-scale problem, the paper introduces the GMSConv (Group Multiscale Convolution) module and integrates it into the C2f part of the YOLOv8n network, forming the C2f_GMSConv module, to comprehensively capture and understand defects of varying sizes.Finally, during the model training process, the Inner EIoU is used as the loss function to optimize the precision of bounding box regression and to accelerate model convergence. Experimental results on the NEU-DET dataset show that the improved model achieves an mAP@0.5 of 80.6%, which is a 4.1% increase over the original model. This model meets the requirements for accurate detection and identification of steel surface defects.

articleTitle: Classification of Mammogram Analysis Using BL-CNN
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: One of the methods currently available for breast cancer screening is mammography, which can be used to detect lesions related to breast cancer. It is known that tumors can occur in any part of the breast, and that a single breast may have multiple lesion instances. It can be challenging to identify multiple suspicious locations and classify them appropriately in the meantime. To tackle this problem, we proposed BiLinear-CNN (BL-CNN in short) in which a Mask R-CNN model is used to detect and extract the lesion instances and a bilinear pooling model to classify them as benign and malignant.
