BL-CNN can identify the suspicious regions of a single breast with a confidence score and classify them as either benign or malignant in the meantime. The Mask R-CNN part of BL-CNN is pretrained with COCO Dataset for lesion instance detection, and the Bilinear Pooling part is pretrained with ImageNet dataset for classification. The models are fine tuned with breast cancer mammography dataset. Experiments on two breast cancer datasets CBIS-DDSM and Inbreast have shown the effectiveness of our model. This model achieved 90% AUC and 95.58% overall accuracy performance over the SegNet segmentation model and U-Net CNN encode and decoder architecture.

articleTitle: Multi-view Ensemble Clustering Based on BLS-Autoencoder
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: With the richness of data sources, data from various modalities reflect the features of samples from different views. To uncover the cluster structure of these data in an unsupervised setting, multi-view clustering approaches have garnered extensive attention. However, the current multi-view clustering approaches usually learn a shared data representation or graph embedding for the final clustering process, which may lead to the loss of view-specific information. Therefore, in this paper, we propose a multi-view ensemble clustering framework based on BLS-autoencoder(MVEC-BLSAE). In generation phase, a multi-view BLS-autoencoder(MVBLSAE) considering both the cross-view subspace structure and the within-view feature projection is designed, which can extract compressed feature subspaces and contribute to producing multiple basic partitions. In integration phase, based on the basic partitions, the sample-cluster relevance is captured through computing fuzzy partition matrices, which are then leveraged to achieve a better consensus partition via graph-cut algorithm on the constructed bipartite graph. According to the experimental results of parameters analysis, comparative analysis and ablation study, MVEC-BLSAE achieves more satisfactory performance compared to several existing multi-view clustering approaches.

articleTitle: A Time Series Analysis-Based Forest Disturbance Time Backtracking Method in Northeastern China, the Changbai Mountain
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Forest disturbance is a crucial factor in evaluating carbon sink changes in ecological studies. Current research on forest disturbances mainly focuses on forest disturbance detection, forest disturbance classification, and other analyses and statistics of forest changes methods. These studies are mostly based on time-series images or forest remote sensing features to achieve dynamic monitoring of forest changes. However, it is often impossible to construct disturbance information with a lack of images from early remote sensing. This paper addresses this limitation by proposes a method of forest disturbance time backtracking which can get historical information on forest disturbance over a wider temporal distribution. Using this method, we ultimately achieved forest disturbance detection on early remote sensing images from the 1960s. This method is based on machine learning and deep learning algorithms to construct two forest disturbance datasets to achieve this goal. The first dataset, for categorizing forest disturbances, is the first of its kind in Northeast China. This data can be widely used in similar studies. The second dataset is the forest disturbance recovery year dataset. We estimate the timing of early forest disturbance by classifying this dataset. The experimental results showed that the first dataset has an accuracy of over 90%, and the backtracking historical disturbance results are consistent with the actual historical information. This method is significant in its ability to fill in gaps in the forest disturbance classification present in Northeast China and enhance the confidence and time span of the forest disturbance detection method.

articleTitle: Research on Cross-Platform Motion Control System Based on gSOAP
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Traditional industrial motion control systems usually use local PCs to connect with the controller through cables. For the shortcomings of this kind of control system, such as strong platform dependence and restricted control territory, a generalized motion control system that can be cross-platform and more flexible in application is proposed. Firstly, the WebService service of controller API is generated by gSOAP tool and deployed on Linux system containing real-time preemption patch PREEMPT_RT, and the communication between non-real-time and real-time processes of API instruction call is completed by naming FIFO, and the functions of control instruction parsing, motion control interpolation and axis output control are completed. Finally, experiments show that the motion control system based on gSOAP can realize reliable cross-platform and cross-region control connection, and the human-computer interaction interface can be quickly customized at any time according to the demand without being limited to any device. The new motion control system operates in a more flexible and efficient way, and can better meet the development needs of personalized, intelligent and flexible production.

articleTitle: Inertial Projectile Trajectory Estimation Method Based on Conv-LSTM and Particle Filtering Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: The development of trajectory parameter estimation methods only based on inertial sensors under GNSS-denied scenarios plays a crucial role in enhancing the survivability of projectile correction ammunition. To alleviate the accumulation of inertial errors during flight, we propose an integrated framework that combines neural networks and particle filters. Specifically, a Conv-LSTM network is employed to learn the dynamic model of the projectile using inertial sensor data and initial trajectory parameters. The predictions generated by the network are then utilized in the particle filter for measurement correction. Furthermore, a simplified strapdown inertial navigation solution model and error model are constructed specifically for close-range correction ammunition, while the latter is employed for state update. The impact of inertial sensor noise and untrained launch angles on the prediction performance is evaluated. The simulation results demonstrate that the dual correction mechanism effectively overcomes the limitations of the traditional Dead-Reckoning algorithm. and maintains a higher level of measurement accuracy over an extended time period, which highlights the promising potential for projectile correction applications.

articleTitle: Bacterial Inhibition Zone Recognition Method Based on YOLO
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing involves placing antibiotic-containing paper disks on bacterial culture media surfaces. These drugs affect bacterial growth, resulting in inhibition zones that reflect the bacteria's sensitivity to the drug. Therefore, using digital means for intelligent identification of inhibition zone size is of great practical significance. This article proposes a deep learning model based on the YOLO target detection algorithm, capable of automatically identifying inhibition zones. Firstly, we load the pre-trained YOLO model and classify the output candidate boxes into several categories: petri dish, inhibition zone, and paper disk. This adaptation makes the YOLO model suitable for our task of inhibition zone recognition. Next, we use processed inhibition zone images to train the pre-trained YOLO model. We then evaluate the performance of multiple YOLO models and determine the optimal values for relevant hyperparameters to enhance overall performance. Experimental results show that, compared to other YOLO algorithms, the model trained using the YOLov9 algorithm achieves optimal performance in recognizing inhibition zones. Based on the recognition results, OpenCV tools are used to precisely calculate the diameter of inhibition zones and further assess antimicrobial efficacy. Finally, we developed an intelligent mobile application that allows researchers to automatically measure the diameter of inhibition zones and evaluate antibacterial capabilities using mobile devices. This application enables more efficient antimicrobial susceptibility analysis and accelerates antibacterial drug research.

articleTitle: Unify and Boost Token for Multi-Modal Person Re-Identification
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Multi-modal person re-identification aims to match images of the same pedestrian captured by different cameras at different locations, utilizing multiple modalities of the pedestrian's images. The advantage of multi-modal images lies in their ability to provide complementary information between modalities, thereby alleviating the problem of insufficient representation caused by factors such as lighting in single-modal images. Recent works have shown that fusing multi-modal features can improve the performance of models in person re-identification tasks. However, most of these works do not narrow the distribution gap between modalities before fusing the features, and they do not fully exploit the information provided by local features during the fusion stage. Therefore, we propose a multi-modal person re-identification framework that utilizes trainable prototypes to integrate and align tokens extracted from various modalities by Vision Transformers before employing a multi-head cross-modal attention mechanism for cross-modal interaction. The framework consists of three parts: Baseline Feature Extraction based on Vision Transformers, Local Feature Alignment Learning Module, and Attention-guided Cross-domain Fusion Module. Firstly, Baseline Feature Extraction based on Vision Transformers comprehensively extracts various features from each modality to avoid information loss. Secondly, Local Feature Alignment Learning Module integrates and aligns the tokens extracted from each modality, reducing redundancy in the information. Finally, the aligned tokens are further enhanced in their feature representation and robustness through Attention-guided Cross-domain Fusion Module. Experimental results on the RGBNT201 dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed approach, achieving promising performance compared to existing methods in recent works.

articleTitle: Semi-Supervised Multi-View Ensemble Clustering with Subspaces Extraction and Constraints Propagation
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: Semi-supervised multi-view clustering extends the principles of multi-modal analysis by focusing on the partitioning of data into distinct groups based on limited number of pairwise constraints. Guided by pairwise constraints, the existing methods suffer from a lack of integration at the level of view-specific subspaces and partitions, which may lead to information loss of each view. In order to sovle this problem, this paper proposes a semi-supervised multi-view ensemble clustering framework with subspaces extraction and constraints propagation (SSMVEC). For each view, a constrained multi-view broad self-encoding network (CMVBSN) is firstly designed to integrate cross-view affinity, within-view projection and pairwise constraints to extract a compressed feature subspace and derive a base partition. By absorbing the information from both pairwise constraints and multiple partitions, the bidirectional constraint propagation is adopted to refines the unified similarity matrix. Finally, the graph-cut algorithm is applied to obtain the consensus partition. Demonstrated by the analysis of parameters, comparison methods and incremental constraints on multiple multi-view datasets, SSMVEC can effectively leverage pairwise constraints and achieve overall better performance than several multi-view clustering methods.

articleTitle: CMDM: A Control Motion Diffusion Model for 2D Digital Human Motion Video Generation
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: In recent years, 2D digital human motion generation (DHMG) is becoming increasingly crucial for many areas such as virtual live broadcasting and film production. Although a lot of effort has been invested in DHMG, the complexity and diversity of human movements make it difficult to generate motions for arbitrary poses, and it is challenging to avoid distortion in the generated hand regions. To address these challenges, in this paper, we propose Control Motion Diffusion Model (CMDM), a diffusion based method for generating 2D digital human motion videos with arbitrary given poses. In CMDM, a novel Pose Control Module (PCM) is customized to fully encode pose and character information, generating multi-level and multi-resolution embedding, thereby ensuring that the model can learn more precise human motion features. In addition, data augmentation and VAE fine-tuning training strategies are adopted to decouple character and pose features, improving the model's ability to generate unseen poses. Finally, comprehensive experiments have been completed to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method, and the proposed CMDM has achieved significant improvement in both subjective and objective evaluations.

articleTitle: Exoskeleton Human-Computer Interaction Based on Deep Learning and sEMG Imaging
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI)
abstract: This research develops an optimized exoskeleton design for human-robot interaction, using surface electromyography (sEMG) to detect patient movement intentions and motor functions. The study involved rapid identification of human gait events, joint angles, and movements, using data from six individuals performing various movements on a 3D force platform. The exoskeleton and motion analysis system (MAS) processed this data, which was utilized for model training and validation. The evaluation was conducted using Root-mean-square error (RMSE) and Correlation Coefficient (CC). We introduced a novel sEMG analysis method leveraging deep and integrated learning to directly classify sEMG signals, achieving high classification accuracy (AUC of 0.9554). A fast-training classification technique utilizing motor-related cortical potentials and varied neural oscillations also exceeded the accuracy of existing classifiers, effectively supporting joint motion recognition and prediction. The optimized exoskeleton provides a viable and safe rehabilitation alternative for patients with neurological disabilities, offering a potential replacement for conventional therapies.
